Exact rule: CONFIRMS RAO-JTC-035 — "This gives those planets strength as if they were in their own houses. This is one of the most powerful Yogas." And adds five things Rao does not: 1. Jupiter, Saturn, Rahu or Ketu in exchange → long-lasting results. 4. A combust planet in exchange loses its combustion. 5. Two debilitated planets in exchange can be beneficial (e.g. Mars in Cancer ↔ Moon in Scorpio). But "an exalted planet can be weakened by enemy planets when undergoing exchange."

Rule description: APUTRA YOGA — the absence of a male child

The Sun boxed in ⇒ "in the REAR sign of the Sun is placed Venus and Moon, and SECOND to the Sun there is Saturn and Mercury — therefore the Sun is quite helpless, because he is under the control of Rahu. Exact rule: The book names the two nodes differently when each pairs with Mars, and the two names are thematically distinct, not interchangeable: - Mars + Ketu → a SERPENT-themed curse: "Sarpa Dosha" / "Sarpa Shapa" (serpent affliction), carrying a karmic-debt/ancestral-transgression framing. Chart 48 (p. 234) names the specific remedy: "Shanti rituals under the guidance of a Kashyapa Gotra Brahmin priest." - Mars + Rahu → an ANCESTOR-themed curse: "Pitru Dosha" (curse of ancestors, Chart 46) or "Pitamaha Shapa" (grandfather's curse, Chart 53) — explicitly tied to a male-ancestor lineage rather than a serpentine/karmic-debt framing.
Effect of the rule: The book names the two nodes differently when each pairs with Mars, and the two names are thematically distinct, not interchangeable: - Mars + Ketu → a SERPENT-themed curse: "Sarpa Dosha" / "Sarpa Shapa" (serpent affliction), carrying a karmic-debt/ancestral-transgression framing. Chart 48 (p. 234) names the specific remedy: "Shanti rituals under the guidance of a Kashyapa Gotra Brahmin priest." - Mars + Rahu → an ANCESTOR-themed curse: "Pitru Dosha" (curse of ancestors, Chart 46) or "Pitamaha Shapa" (grandfather's curse, Chart 53) — explicitly tied to a male-ancestor lineage rather than a serpentine/karmic-debt framing.
Combination of the rule: Mars conjoined or directionally paired with one lunar node.

Rule description: MATRU DOSHA / MATRU SHAPA / MATHRU SHAPA — one doctrine, three names
Exact rule: All three spellings/names (Matru Dosha, Matru Shaap, Mathru Shapa) describe the same doctrine: a karmically-loaded maternal-lineage affliction, read off a weak or surrounded Moon. Effects named across instances: emotional instability, unresolved maternal/ancestral karma, delayed or denied marriage, and a recommended remedy of Shanti Kriyas specifically for the Moon (and whichever malefic co-occupies/afflicts it).
Effect of the rule: All three spellings/names (Matru Dosha, Matru Shaap, Mathru Shapa) describe the same doctrine: a karmically-loaded maternal-lineage affliction, read off a weak or surrounded Moon. Effects named across instances: emotional instability, unresolved maternal/ancestral karma, delayed or denied marriage, and a recommended remedy of Shanti Kriyas specifically for the Moon (and whichever malefic co-occupies/afflicts it).
Combination of the rule: Moon afflicted — typically Moon+Ketu conjunction, or Moon conjunct Mars with additional nodal/malefic pressure from the directional trine.

Rule description: GANDHARVA KALA YOGA — Rahu linking Moon and Venus together (artistic-talent yoga)
Exact rule: "The influence of Rahu on both Moon and Venus forms what is traditionally known as Gandharva Kala Yoga, often seen in charts of individuals gifted in music, drama, and the performing arts." This is a NEW named yoga, not attested elsewhere in the BNN corpus surveyed so far (not in RAO/ARI/AVA/NEO/GUP rule files). Distinguishes a specific Rahu-as-connector configuration from Rahu's usual disruptive signification.
Effect of the rule: "The influence of Rahu on both Moon and Venus forms what is traditionally known as Gandharva Kala Yoga, often seen in charts of individuals gifted in music, drama, and the performing arts." This is a NEW named yoga, not attested elsewhere in the BNN corpus surveyed so far (not in RAO/ARI/AVA/NEO/GUP rule files). Distinguishes a specific Rahu-as-connector configuration from Rahu's usual disruptive signification.
Combination of the rule: Rahu stands in directional/trinal relationship to both Moon and Venus simultaneously (Rahu in Scorpio, Moon in the 5th from it, Venus+Sun in the 9th from it, in the worked chart).

Rule description: KUMBHA-MUSTI YOGA — Mars in Aquarius, surrounded by its own enemies
Exact rule: "Mars occupies the sign of Aquarius (Kumbha), forming Kumbha-Musti Yoga. It is in conjunction with Saturn and Mercury, both of whom are natural enemies of Mars." Named yoga for Mars being metaphorically "a fist closed against itself" — strong by occupying a sign, powerless by the company it keeps. NEW named yoga, not previously attested in the corpus.
Effect of the rule: "Mars occupies the sign of Aquarius (Kumbha), forming Kumbha-Musti Yoga. It is in conjunction with Saturn and Mercury, both of whom are natural enemies of Mars." Named yoga for Mars being metaphorically "a fist closed against itself" — strong by occupying a sign, powerless by the company it keeps. NEW named yoga, not previously attested in the corpus.
Combination of the rule: Mars occupies Aquarius (Kumbha) in conjunction with planets inimical to Mars (here: Saturn and Mercury).

Rule description: "KALAPURUSHA'S MOUTH" — Murthy's recurring literary device for Rahu/nodal drain, not a technical dosha
Exact rule: Across 9+ occurrences, Murthy uses "mouth of Kalapurusha," "Kalapurusha Dosha," and "agent of Kalapurusha" as interchangeable poetic framing for a single mechanical idea already in the corpus: a directionally/trinally-linked Rahu neutralizes or absorbs the planet(s) it touches, whether they are benefic or malefic. Verdict: this is an author idiom, not a distinct technical dosha — once at p. 117 it is dignified with "Dosha" in the name, but the underlying condition and effect are identical to the plain "Rahu directionally afflicts X" statements used everywhere else without the label.
Effect of the rule: Across 9+ occurrences, Murthy uses "mouth of Kalapurusha," "Kalapurusha Dosha," and "agent of Kalapurusha" as interchangeable poetic framing for a single mechanical idea already in the corpus: a directionally/trinally-linked Rahu neutralizes or absorbs the planet(s) it touches, whether they are benefic or malefic. Verdict: this is an author idiom, not a distinct technical dosha — once at p. 117 it is dignified with "Dosha" in the name, but the underlying condition and effect are identical to the plain "Rahu directionally afflicts X" statements used everywhere else without the label.
Combination of the rule: Any planet positioned such that Rahu (or occasionally a retrograde planet in its own sign) directionally "swallows," "absorbs," or "drains" it.

Rule description: Venus is the wife; Mars is the husband
Exact rule: A gender-switched karaka, and it must not be missed. - Male chart — "Venus representing the native's partner is conjunct Jupiter" (Ch 5). - Female chart — "In this chart of a female … The planet indicating the partner (Mars) is conjunct Rahu" (Ch 24).
Effect of the rule: The spouse's character, fortune and troubles are read from that planet by the standard frame (RAO-FND-009).

Rule description: In a female chart the Sun gives children
Exact rule: "…the Sun who gives children has to cross over Saturn, Moon and Ketu and reach the next house."
Effect of the rule: The number, timing and quality of children. Here, the Sun crossing Saturn, Moon and Ketu gives "an ordinary one with mediocre means of livelihood."
Combination of the rule: Female native; children are to be read.

Rule description: Venus in a Mars sign: the partner comes from the native place
Exact rule: "As Venus is in the house of Mars, his partner will come from his native place."
Effect of the rule: A bride from the native's own region.
Combination of the rule: Venus occupies a sign owned by Mars.

Rule description: Jupiter in the 12th to Venus: an unhappy first marriage
Exact rule: "As regards the married life, Jupiter in 12th to Venus indicates unhappy first marriage — thereafter, he will be happy."
Effect of the rule: First marriage unhappy; happiness after.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter stands in the 12th from Venus.

Rule description: Venus among enemies, with the Moon in her 12th: domestic unhappiness
Exact rule: "Though born in a good family, his domestic life is not happy as Venus is in conjunction with the Sun and Jupiter who are enemies and the Moon is in 12th to Venus."
Effect of the rule: Domestic unhappiness in an otherwise well-born life.
Combination of the rule: Venus conjunct the Sun and Jupiter, "who are enemies", and the Moon in the 12th to Venus.

Rule description: A blemish on Venus by exchange: the wife deceived
Exact rule: "Venus representing the native's partner is conjunct Jupiter who has exchange of signs with the Moon in Sagittarius. So, there is a blemish on Venus and the native's wife being duped had relations with a person other than her husband."
Effect of the rule: The wife deceived into a relationship outside the marriage.
Combination of the rule: Venus conjunct Jupiter, and Jupiter has an exchange of signs with the Moon.

Rule description: Mars conjunct Venus, and the Moon's movement: elopement
Exact rule: The Master answers the disciple's objection "what does Mars do? Will he be inactive?" by ordering the events: "With Mars-Venus conjunction before the transit of the Moon in Taurus, the native's wife would have given birth to a male child and only later she goes away."
Effect of the rule: A son first, then elopement, then hard years, then return and reconciliation, and the native "will live upto a good old age of 72."
Combination of the rule: Mars conjunct Venus in Taurus (Venus's own sign); the Moon moves to join them, having "received air from Saturn" — Saturn being debilitated and "the opponent of Mars".

Rule description: Rahu about to fall upon Venus: widowhood
Exact rule: "Here, Rahu is about to pounce upon Venus. This indicates a widow. Venus, before transiting Libra, will contact the Moon at the same point, and so the widow would be a relation of the mother of the native."
Effect of the rule: A widow connected to the mother's side of the family.
Combination of the rule: Rahu stands in the sign after Venus — and so, moving backwards (RAO-JTC-013), is about to arrive on her.

Rule description: Marriage timed by Jupiter conjunct Venus and Mars
Exact rule: "In this chart of a female, Jupiter is conjunct Venus and Mars. So the native will be married in her 12th year. Rahu also is in the same house and when he transits Taurus or Aquarius the partner will have considerable trouble."
Effect of the rule: Very early marriage; a troubled partner; an ordinary son.
Combination of the rule: Female chart; Jupiter conjunct Venus and Mars, with Rahu in the same sign; Venus and Saturn have exchanged signs.

Rule description: Children counted and characterised from what follows Jupiter
Exact rule: The forward-is-younger convention (RAO-FND-024) applied to children: - Ch 17 — "With Venus and the Sun following Jupiter's position, it is likely that two of the children will have good earning and they will achieve great fame. Mercury and Rahu being followed by the Sun, it is likely that one of the children will settle down in a foreign country." - Ch 25 — "The combination in Leo indicates 3 children. But one boy and one girl will be able to live a very ordinary poor life." - Ch 16 — the Moon exalted with Ketu in the next house gives "a large family of 9 children."
Effect of the rule: Number, sex, prosperity and dispersal of the children.
Combination of the rule: The planets standing after Jupiter's sign are read in order.

Rule description: Children's profession follows the parent's significators
Exact rule: "His children will be in medical profession or dedicate their lives to Vedic culture" (Ch 19, where Jupiter and Ketu stand in the 7th to Saturn and the native lives by propitiation). "He will have one daughter and 2 boys and they will take up his own profession" (Ch 20).
Effect of the rule: The children's field of work.

Rule description: Siblings counted from the karaka's neighbours and its 7th and 10th
Exact rule: "Mars in his own house Scorpio with Jupiter in 7th from him, Venus in 8th and Mercury and Rahu in 10th — the native will have 5 or 6 brothers and sisters" (Ch 17). Chart 18 likewise gives "5-6 brothers and sisters." Compare RAO-FND-026, where the count is taken from Jupiter's first round instead.
Effect of the rule: The number of brothers and sisters.
Combination of the rule: Mars is taken as the sibling karaka and the standard frame applied.

Rule description: Many inimical planets: siblings born but not surviving
Exact rule: "This native will have many brothers and sisters, but very few will live long as there are many inimical forces combined" (Ch 6). "His brothers and sisters will have to face some trouble (Mars and the Moon next to Rahu)" (Ch 13).
Effect of the rule: Many siblings, few surviving.
Combination of the rule: "many inimical forces combined" around the sibling karakas; or Mars and the Moon standing next to Rahu.

Rule description: No planet behind Jupiter: the native is the eldest
Exact rule: "As Jupiter has no place in the previous house and there is Ketu in Leo, he happens to be the eldest (first born)."
Effect of the rule: The native is the first-born.
Combination of the rule: The sign before Jupiter's is empty, and Ketu stands elsewhere.

Rule description: The mother read from the Moon's sign, company and neighbours
Exact rule: Four contrasting readings, from the same frame: - Ch 9 — "The representative of mother, the Moon, is in Virgo. She will be beautiful and the Sun in the Moon's exaltation sign shows her faithfulness to husband." - Ch 13 — "As the Moon is placed in her own house and conjunct Mars, Rahu being behind him, the mother of the native will have some troubles in her life." - Ch 3 — the Moon conjunct Saturn, Saturn–Mars in exchange, the Moon taking the Daityamsa from Mars conjunct Rahu → the mother's misconduct. - Ch 7 — "When Saturn transits Libra the mother will suffer ill-health."
Effect of the rule: The mother's beauty, fidelity, health and troubles.
Combination of the rule: The Moon is taken as karaka and the standard frame applied.

Rule description: A planet standing between two karakas breaks the relation between them
Exact rule: "Further, between Jupiter (the child in question) and the Sun (father), there is Venus in the middle in the child's horoscope. Hence, the relationship between father and child will not be very happy (Jupiter and Venus are enemies)."
Effect of the rule: Estrangement between the two people whose karakas are separated.
Combination of the rule: A planet occupies a sign between the karakas of two family members, and it is an enemy of one of them.

Rule description: Grandparents and inherited property read from the further neighbours
Exact rule: "The grandfather of the native had wealth and landed property (Mercury-Venus in the house adjoining to Rahu's position) and the Sun's conjunction with Mercury and Venus indicating the parents to have inherited the properties and passed it on to the native. But the father lost all property on account of his quarrelsome nature, and his sister being left without children he came to possess that property."
Effect of the rule: Ancestral property lost by the father and recovered by another route; Saturn–Rahu conjunction gives "wind troubles to the parents", and "the old house owned by the father will be demolished."
Combination of the rule: Mercury and Venus in the sign adjoining Rahu's; the Sun conjunct Mercury and Venus; Jupiter and Saturn in exchange.

Rule description: Each sibling IS a planet, and is read by its own frame
Exact rule: The most important extension of the sibling census in the whole batch. Rao does not merely count siblings — he identifies each with a planet and then reads that planet's own frame as if it were a native: - Ch 54 — "One of the brothers will be a dogged type, have medium education and have no one to help him. The second brother is represented by Mercury, who has Saturn and Ketu next to him. This brother will have mental aberrations." - Ch 42 — "In between Saturn and Jupiter there is Mars. Hence, one of his brothers will have short life. … Mars is Lord of the 4th and the 11th from Jupiter. Hence, there will be accrual of money through the brother." - Ch 41 — "One of his brothers will attain great fame (Mars, Mercury and Jupiter in consecutive houses)." - Ch 8 (earlier) — the first brother, Mars, with Saturn in his 4th and Ketu in his 6th, "will take up Sanyas" (RAO-PBR-009).
Effect of the rule: A separate biography for each sibling.
Combination of the rule: The planets Jupiter crosses after his own sign are taken one by one, each as a named sibling in birth order (RAO-FND-026).

Rule description: Nothing behind Jupiter: the eldest — and Ketu does not count
Exact rule: Stated three more times, and once with a crucial exception spelled out: - Ch 27 — "As Jupiter has no planets behind him, the native will be the eldest son." - Ch 54 — "As there are no planets behind Jupiter, he has no elder brothers. He will have 5 or 6 brothers and sisters all younger to him." - Ch 44 — "As there are no planets behind Jupiter except Ketu, the native had no elder brothers and so he was the eldest born."
Effect of the rule: The native is first-born.
Combination of the rule: No planets in the sign before Jupiter's.

Rule description: Two wives: the dual sign, or Venus and the Moon framing Jupiter
Exact rule: The dual sign — Ch 35, "Venus in the dual sign Gemini indicates two wives." - The Moon in Jupiter's 6th, Venus in his 11th — Ch 34, "With Venus in Cancer, Leo vacant, and Jupiter in Virgo two marriages are indicated. The reason is that the Moon is in 6th to Jupiter and Venus occupies the 11th from Jupiter." Rao gives his reasoning explicitly, which is rare. - Venus contacting Rahu with Ketu next to Jupiter — Ch 39, "He will marry one woman as Venus is in Aquarius, and will have contact with another family woman when Venus contacts Rahu, as Jupiter has Ketu in the next house to him."
Effect of the rule: Two marriages, or one marriage and an outside connection.
Combination of the rule: Three distinct routes to the same verdict, all in this batch:

Rule description: The same chart read for either sex
Exact rule: Rao writes out both readings side by side, from one chart: "If the native be a male, he will be well educated, employed in the field of machinery and will occupy a high post. He may not have a happy married life. If she be a woman, she will not be happy with her husband. The partner will be entangled in quarrel with enemies and will experience misery." Chart 31 does the same, appending "Female native will be married in her 18th year…" to a male reading.
Effect of the rule: Two parallel readings from one set of placements.
Combination of the rule: The sex of the native is not fixed.

Rule description: Which planet stands for the partner can be decided by placement
Exact rule: "The Master answers that there is a special Yoga here. Here Mars is posited in the sign of Venus. So Venus represents the partner for this native."
Effect of the rule: With Venus in Leo, the Sun's own sign, "he will elope with someone's wife and will have a child by her"; the Moon between the Sun and Venus shows "the whole affair to be a planned one of seduction", and the Moon in the 2nd to Venus shows "the progeny of the lover." Catalogued, not endorsed.
Combination of the rule: The disciple asks whether the native will marry at all, given Mars conjunct the Sun.

Rule description: The wife's character and health read from Venus's frame
Exact rule: The recursive method of RAO-DOM-018, turned on the wife: | Chart | Configuration | The wife | |---|---|---| | Ch 50 | Jupiter and the Sun next to Venus | "the partner of a devotional nature and a very capable woman" | | Ch 54 | Venus–Mercury conjunction, Ketu in the 2nd to them | "his wife will be a dullard with poor memory" | | Ch 42 | Venus conjunct Ketu, with debilitated inimical Jupiter | "The partner will be a religious lady and beautiful. She will face abortions." | | Ch 58 | Venus conjunct Rahu | "he will have daughters instead of sons" | | Ch 41 | — | "His wife will not have a full measure of health. She may be suffering from piles and urinary trouble." | | Ch 59 | Venus has the Sun next to him and Mars in the next house from the Sun | "disappointments will be his lot"; the wife "of a dogged type"
Effect of the rule: A description of the spouse as a person.
Combination of the rule: Venus is taken as the karaka and the standard frame applied to her.

Rule description: Distance with nothing in between: separation and loss
Exact rule: The emptiness rule (RAO-PRF-012) applied to relationships: - Ch 41 — "His mother will predecease her husband (Rahu in Cancer far away from Venus with no planets in between)." - Ch 41 — "As Venus meets the Moon next after meeting Rahu, the mother witnesses the passing away of a daughter." - Ch 60 — "As Mars is inimical to Saturn and Venus, the native will not see his father for a long time and will have no brothers. The combination of the Sun and Venus denies him sisters also." - Ch 45 — "Since the second house to the Sun is aspected by Jupiter the native will migrate from his native place of birth."
Effect of the rule: Estrangement, distance, migration, or bereavement.
Combination of the rule: Two karakas stand far apart with no planet between them; or a planet stands between two karakas (RAO-DOM-016).

Rule description: Children counted by naming the planets
Exact rule: Rao names them individually, exactly as he does for siblings (RAO-DOM-018): - Ch 42 — "The native will have 3 boys (Sun, Jupiter and Mars), who may not be long lived. His daughters will not survive." - Ch 48 — "He will have three daughters on account of Saturn-Ketu conjunction and Venus aspected by the Moon in conjunction with Jupiter. Because Jupiter being posited in his own house he will be blessed with one boy." - Ch 33 — "As the Sun has Venus-Mercury combination next to him, he will have 3 to 4 children including daughters."
Effect of the rule: The number and sex of children.
Combination of the rule: The planets in the relevant frame are counted, and each is assigned to a child.

Rule description: The mother rules, stated by Rao as explicit conditionals
Exact rule: The single most valuable passage in this batch. Rao almost always reasons from a particular chart; here he stops and states three general rules in bare if-then form, then applies them: > "If the Moon be not placed either in 2nd or 7th from the Sun, the mother will be living > separately. If the Moon be with Rahu, mother will be disease ridden. In the above > circumstances, as lonely Mars is outside the Rahu-Ketu orbit, one should predict that the > mother is in love with someone other than her husband."
Effect of the rule: Mother living apart; mother ill; or estrangement in the parents' marriage.

Rule description: The 5th from Jupiter gives the children
Exact rule: "In the 5th house to Jupiter, Sun-Mercury and Ketu are posited. So he will have 2 male and 2 female issues."
Effect of the rule: The number and sex of children.
Combination of the rule: Planets occupy the 5th house from Jupiter.

Rule description: Two wives for the father: five separate routes
Exact rule: The commonest single verdict in this stretch of the book — Rao returns to it in eleven charts, by five different routes: | Route | Statement | Chart | |---|---|---| | Female planets in the sign after the Sun | "The native's father will have 2 wives as female planets occupy the succeeding house" | Ch 69 | | The lord of the 7th from the Sun in a dual sign | "As the Moon, Lord of 7th from the Sun, is in Gemini, a dual sign, the native's father will have 2 marriages" | Ch 83 | | Parivartana of Sun and Mars, with planets between | "The Sun and Mars have exchanged places … the Moon in between the Sun and Mars. So the father is likely to have two marriages" | Ch 81 | | Sun–Ketu with Mercury–Venus in the 2nd | "indicates 2 or 3 marriages for the father" | Ch 90 | | The 7th lord from the Sun in the 2nd, and the 5th lord in the 7th | "This indicates one marriage for father and his attachment to another woman also" | Ch 78
Effect of the rule: A second marriage in the father's life, or an outside attachment.
Combination of the rule: Various, all in the Sun's or the Moon's frame.

Rule description: An empty 2nd and 7th from Mars: no family happiness
Exact rule: Ch 67 — "He will not have family happiness as there are no planets in the succeeding house or the opposite house of Mars." - Ch 85 — "The father will have little marital happiness as there are no planets on either side of Ketu-Mars." - Ch 87 — "He will have no harmony in his family life on account of presence of the Moon behind Venus."
Effect of the rule: A marriage without warmth.
Combination of the rule: No planets in the sign after, or the 7th from, Mars — or none on either side of the Ketu–Mars pair.

Rule description: Counting relatives by counting planets in the frame
Exact rule: The corpus uses several counting devices side by side. Collected here because they do not always agree, and a reader must know which is being used: | Method | Worked instance | Chart | |---|---|---| | Planets in the 7th + parivartana + the 3rd | "Mars … has 3 planets in the 7th from his position … parivartana with Mercury … and one planet in the 3rd. This indicates Ekadasa Sahodara (11 brothers)" | Ch 69 | | Exalted Venus | "As Venus is in exaltation the native will have many sisters (say about 5)" | Ch 70 | | The Sun's associates | "The Sun has two associates viz. Mercury and Mars. The father had 3 brothers." | Ch 98 | | Venus in the 7th to Jupiter | "indicates a younger sister" | Ch 73 | | Nothing in the 12th from Jupiter | "the native will have one elder sister" | Ch 71
Effect of the rule: The number of brothers and sisters, and their seniority.
Combination of the rule: Planets in a karaka's frame are counted.

Rule description: Angaraka Dosha delays marital happiness
Exact rule: "This native has Angaraka Dosha (Mars in Aries). This will delay marital happiness. Things will get better from 25th year upto 63rd year."
Effect of the rule: Marital happiness postponed.

Rule description: Marriage timed to the taking up of a job
Exact rule: "Venus contacts Saturn first and Rahu next. So the native gets married when he takes up a job."
Effect of the rule: Marriage and employment arriving together.
Combination of the rule: Venus contacts Saturn first and Rahu next in her forward movement.

Rule description: The three sibling planets: Venus, Mars and Mercury
Exact rule: Rao names them outright, which he has not done before: "The planets which indicate brothers and sisters i.e. Venus, Mars and Mercury are all in Scorpio. The next house is occupied by Saturn and Moon. As Venus contacts Saturn first and later Rahu in his movements, so the sisters cannot enjoy married life for long." And Ch 147: "The significator of brothers Mars is conjunct with inimical Rahu. Therefore something will be wrong with a brother."
Effect of the rule: The siblings' number, sex and fortunes.

Rule description: Marriage delayed, denied, or multiplied
Exact rule: The corpus's four distinct marriage-verdicts, each with its own signature: | Verdict | Signature | Statement | Chart | |---|---|---|---| | Delayed, and out of turn | Venus in the 12th to Mars | "denotes delay in marriage and he will permit his younger brother to marry earlier than himself. All sisters and brothers will get married first and the native will marry last" | Ch 151 | | Denied | Saturn contacting Ketu in his rounds | "this will deny marriage to the native" | Ch 137 | | Doubled | Saturn contacting Ketu then Venus, fighting Venus in the 6th | "there is a double marriage yoga. Even this will not bring happiness" | Ch 121 | | Tripled | Mars with Venus in the 2nd, Jupiter in the 3rd, Ketu in the 4th | "the native will have 2-3 wives" (Ch 136); Ch 141 gives three in fact — "married at 21 or 24 … again at 32, and at 34 his 3rd wife" | Ch 136, 141
Effect of the rule: Marriage delayed, denied, or repeated.

Rule description: Birth by operation, read from the Moon's company
Exact rule: "Jupiter is with Venus, Mars and the Moon — all in Taurus. The Moon is exalted here. He receives power from Venus and Mars situated in the same house. The birth of this boy would be after an operation to the mother." Ch 155 gives the same for the native's own child: "he will have a daughter between 44-45 after the wife undergoes a caesarean operation."
Effect of the rule: A surgical birth.
Combination of the rule: The Moon exalted with Venus and Mars in one sign, "receiving power" from them.

Rule description: Marriage delayed by Venus in the 12th from Mars
Exact rule: "As Venus is in the 12th to Mars, and Ketu is conjunct Mars and the Moon is placed in 8th to Mars, the marriage of the native will be delayed and will take place near about 41-42."
Effect of the rule: Marriage very late, and out of turn among the siblings.
Combination of the rule: Venus in the 12th from Mars, with Ketu conjunct Mars and the Moon in the 8th from him.

Rule description: Wives and children counted from successive contacts of one karaka
Exact rule: The most elaborate marriage-and-progeny count in the book, and every step is shown: > "When Venus comes to the sensitive point representing 'wife', the native will marry a second > woman. As Venus contacts Jupiter and Saturn before coming in conjunction with the Moon, he > will have two issues through his second wife, and the Moon's contact will end that > chapter. Then comes Ketu's contact stationed in the house of Venus (Taurus). He will then > marry his third wife. Ketu has three planets in the second house. Therefore, the third wife will > have three children."
Effect of the rule: Successive marriages, each with its own count of children.
Combination of the rule: Venus and Jupiter each walk forward, meeting the sensitive points in turn (RAO-KRK-081).

Rule description: The chart read for both sexes, a third and fourth time
Exact rule: Rao writes both readings out again, and this time the divergence is large: > "If the native is a male, he will have two marriages. He will eke out livelihood by trade or > be employed in a treasury … If the native be a woman, she will be facing the separation of > her husband for long periods, as he will be having relations with another woman." Ch 183 does the same: "If the native is a woman the results are as follows: As Venus is having the aspect of Jupiter, she will have high educational qualifications…"
Effect of the rule: Two divergent readings from one set of placements.
Combination of the rule: The sex of the native is not fixed.

Rule description: Full house-lordship analysis, counted from the karaka
Exact rule: The disciple argues from lordship; the Preceptor answers in the same currency — and every house is counted from a PLANET, never from the Lagna: > Disciple: "The lord of the seventh house from Mars is Venus, and Venus is in conjunction > with Mercury. So, when these two are together, the native should obtain at least one wife… Is it > not so?" > Preceptor: "Mercury and Venus are in the second house from Mars, which means that the lord of > the seventh house, Venus, is in conjunction with Mercury, the lord of the 8th and 11th house from > Mars. This indicates that a woman will formally marry him, but will desert the native and > live with a former sweetheart of hers." Ch 243 does the same from Jupiter: "The lord of the seventh house from Jupiter is in the 12th from Jupiter. The lord of the sixth house from Jupiter is in the fifth house with the lord of that house. This clearly indicates that there is no doubt regarding unhappiness in matrimony." Ch 282 from Venus: "Mercury happens to be the lord of the fourth and seventh houses from Venus, and so the native will find happiness from her second husband."
Effect of the rule: A decisive marriage verdict where the simple frame was ambiguous.
Combination of the rule: Marriage is contested and the simple frame gives no clear answer.

Rule description: Marriage besieged: the seventh aspect as an army
Exact rule: The drama of RAO-FND-038 at full stretch, and it is doing real analytical work: > "Venus is in his house of exaltation, happy in the company of his friend Mars. At this time, the > Moon, the enemy of Venus, and Saturn, the enemy of Mars, set forth from the capital with a large > army and started besieging Venus and Mars from the seventh house, Virgo. The happiness of Venus > was shattered. Saturn in his turn completely put to rout Mars — and as an effect of this, the > native will lose her husband. But, due to the benign aspect of the Moon, the native will marry > again."
Effect of the rule: The first marriage destroyed, the second granted.
Combination of the rule: The partner-karaka is aspected from the 7th by its enemies.

Rule description: The sibling count stated as an explicit rule
Exact rule: Rao finally states the rule instead of demonstrating it: > "He will have six brothers and one sister. This is got by the number of planets in, and the > adjoining houses of, the placement of Mars." And the sex convention is confirmed by counting feminine bodies: Ch 405, "Saturn, Venus and the Moon in the house of Mars indicate three sisters for the native. Jupiter's aspect on Mars indicates that the native will have a brother also." Ch 397 uses the same convention for relationships: "Mars conjunct two feminine planets, the Moon and Venus" → relations with two or three women.
Effect of the rule: The number and sex of brothers and sisters.

Rule description: Mercury among enemies: a broken educational career
Exact rule: "Mercury the Karaka of education is in enemy camp meeting Rahu in the 2nd house therefrom and also Mars in the 3rd house. Hence, the native will not have a smooth educational career."
Effect of the rule: Education interrupted, not denied.
Combination of the rule: Mercury in an enemy's sign ("enemy camp"), meeting Rahu in the 2nd from himself and Mars in the 3rd.

Rule description: Mercury conjunct his enemy Mars: trials and disappointments in studies
Exact rule: "His Mercury is in conjunction with Mars (his enemy) and so he will face trials and disappointments in educational career. All the same, with Ketu in Virgo owned by Mercury, the native will be well versed in three languages."
Effect of the rule: A disappointing formal education, but real linguistic attainment.

Rule description: Jupiter contacting his enemies caps education at "medium"
Exact rule: "The native will have only medium education as Jupiter contacts his enemies Mercury, Venus and Ketu around his 12th year."
Effect of the rule: Medium education.
Combination of the rule: In his first round, Jupiter contacts Mercury, Venus and Ketu — his enemies.

Rule description: Mercury in his own sign, or with Venus: the intellectual type
Exact rule: Ch 26 — "Mercury is in his own house Virgo with Venus. The native will be of an intellectual type and will shine well." - Ch 22 — "Jupiter having Mercury in the seventh to his place and Venus in the 8th indicate two sources of happiness. He will have an extraordinary intellect and he will be well read in the Vedic lore." - Ch 5 — "The conjunction of Mercury and Ketu made him intelligent" (RAO-KRK-020).
Effect of the rule: Intellectual distinction and public standing by it — Ch 22, "establish himself in a big place and provide comfort to the public by his intellectual powers."
Combination of the rule: Mercury strong — in his own sign Virgo with Venus, or exalted, or with Ketu.

Rule description: Mercury with Jupiter in the next sign: law
Exact rule: "In this chart Mercury, signifying education, is posited in Aquarius and Jupiter is placed in the next house alongwith the Sun and Ketu. The native will, therefore, be a legal expert, kindly in temperament, and will gain much knowledge in some other subject besides law. He will earn fame."
Effect of the rule: Law, plus a second field of knowledge, plus fame.
Combination of the rule: Mercury in Aquarius, with Jupiter in the next sign alongside the Sun and Ketu.

Rule description: Mercury with Jupiter in the 2nd: mastery of scripture
Exact rule: "This native is born in a noble family. His father and grandfather are men of Vedic learning. As Mercury has Jupiter in the 2nd house, the native also is well versed in Vedic lore. As Jupiter contacts Rahu first in his movement and then Mars, the native also will possess knowledge of Mantras."
Effect of the rule: Vedic scholarship, and knowledge of mantras specifically.
Combination of the rule: Mercury has Jupiter in the 2nd house from him; Jupiter in his movement contacts Rahu first and then Mars.

Rule description: A steady educational career
Exact rule: "The native will have a steady educational career. The Moon and Jupiter aspecting each other make the native a philanthropist who will win over his enemies."
Effect of the rule: Uninterrupted education; a generous nature.
Combination of the rule: No affliction to Mercury noted; Moon and Jupiter aspecting each other.

Rule description: Ordinary education despite intelligence
Exact rule: "The native is intelligent, but will have only ordinary education."
Effect of the rule: Intelligence without formal attainment.
Combination of the rule: Education — intelligence and attainment part company

Rule description: Mars in the 12th to Mercury: broken education
Exact rule: "The native will have a broken education as there is Mars in the 12th house to Mercury. The house next to Mercury is occupied by Jupiter and Ketu. Hence, the native will be intelligent and will have regard for elders" (Ch 41). Ch 40: "Mars conjunct Mercury indicates educational breaks. Even then he will be very intelligent."
Effect of the rule: Interrupted schooling; intelligence intact.
Combination of the rule: Mars in the 12th from Mercury, or Mars conjunct Mercury.

Rule description: The Sun and Saturn in the 2nd to Mercury: obstacles to study
Exact rule: "Though placed in his sign Virgo, the placement of the Sun and Saturn in the second house to Mercury puts obstacles in the path of his studies" (Ch 36). "In the next house the placement of Saturn and Ketu shows impediments in educational career" (Ch 53).
Effect of the rule: Obstructed study despite a well-placed Mercury.
Combination of the rule: The Sun and Saturn occupy the 2nd from Mercury; or Saturn and Ketu stand in the sign next to the education significators.

Rule description: Mercury about to enter his exaltation: kingly honours
Exact rule: "Mercury is in Cancer with Rahu in Leo. Next Mercury enters his exaltation in Virgo (the next house). This shows that the native will receive kingly honours."
Effect of the rule: High honours. In the same chart, "His status will go down when Saturn comes to Gemini" — the fall is timed by the other clock.
Combination of the rule: Mercury stands in the sign immediately before his exaltation, so that his next step forward is into Virgo.

Rule description: The Lagna is not primary
Exact rule: Do not build the reading on the ascendant, its lord, or house-lordships counted from the ascendant. Verbatim: "In the Nadi Granthas, the Lagna is not considered as of primary importance."
Effect of the rule: Houses are counted from a planet, not from the ascendant. The karaka replaces the Lagna as the reference point.
Combination of the rule: Any horoscope taken up for Nadi reading.

Rule description: The one thing Lagna is still good for
Exact rule: "Lagna is helpful to find out the actual position of a planet on a particular day." Use the ascendant only to fix which sign a fast-moving or cusp-standing planet actually occupies, then set the Lagna aside.
Effect of the rule: The ascendant is a clock for resolving planetary position, not a significator.
Combination of the rule: Birth time is uncertain, or a planet stands near a sign boundary.

Rule description: Why sign-position must be pinned exactly
Exact rule: The author's worked warning: a child born at the start of Aries lagna may have the Sun "at the very end of Kanya" (Virgo); by the time the Lagna reaches its 27th degree the Sun has moved into Libra, its debilitation. "When we consider the aspect of father of both the births, we will not get the same result."
Effect of the rule: A single sign-change of one karaka reverses the verdict for that department (here: the father). "Such instances can be multiplied to show how changes take place even within a few hours."
Combination of the rule: Two births on the same day, or births a few hours apart.

Rule description: Dasa is not the timing engine
Exact rule: The author's objection to dasa: "When two deaths occur on the same day, both of them may not have maraka dasa operating for them. The same applies in regard to marriages."
Effect of the rule: Two systems are set aside at the outset — Lagna (RAO-FND-001) and dasa (here). What remains is karaka + sign + transit.
Combination of the rule: An event (death, marriage) is to be timed.

Rule description: The Moon and Mercury may be treated as negligible
Exact rule: Verbatim: "If the horoscopes you take up for study are different from the ones you find in this book, you may consider such variations as the position of the Moon or Mercury negligible in those horoscopes."
Effect of the rule: Charts are matched on the skeleton — Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu.
Combination of the rule: A chart under study resembles a book chart but differs in the position of the Moon or of Mercury.

Rule description: What this book is a compilation of
Exact rule: "I have taken some portions from Nandi Nadi and some from Bhrigu Nadi. I have tried my best to explain the final verdict given in the Nadi for various planetary combinations."
Effect of the rule: The book contains above 500 horoscopes, each with prediction and analysis; some further horoscopes are quoted merely as examples.

Rule description: The book is a grammar, not a lookup table
Exact rule: "Multiplication tables remain the same in principle, but its usage can be diverted into any department of Scientific approach to problems of life. Similarly those who follow the arrangement and understand the principles of the NADI … will be able to apply the principles to any chart they come across."
Effect of the rule: The casebook is training data for the grammar, not an index to be matched literally.
Combination of the rule: A chart not found in the book.

Rule description: Tarka: argument for and against
Exact rule: The author credits Sri H.S. Madhu Rao (Mysore) with initiating him into "the method of 'Tarka' i.e. arguments for and against for arriving at the final Truth by an analytic method." The Chart-1 dialogue is written in exactly this shape: the disciple raises the objection, the Master answers it.
Effect of the rule: Every reading should be stated as claim → objection → answer, as the book does.
Combination of the rule: Two or more configurations bear on the same question.

Rule description: The karaka is the reference point
Exact rule: The author's own step-by-step instruction, verbatim: "Take the causative i.e. karaka planet of the particular aspect you want to study, consider the adjacent houses of that planet and the seventh house therefrom. Then, on the principles you find applied in this book, you will also be able to make correct predictions."
Effect of the rule: The reading procedure is exactly three steps — (1) find the karaka for the matter; (2) read the adjacent signs (the one before and the one after — i.e. the 12th and the 2nd from that planet) and the 7th from it; (3) judge.
Combination of the rule: Any department of life is to be read.

Rule description: Jupiter is the karaka for children
Exact rule: "Here in the Nadis we take into account: (1) Jupiter for births of children."
Effect of the rule: Number, sex and timing of children are read from Jupiter.
Combination of the rule: Births of children are to be read.

Rule description: Mercury is the karaka for education
Exact rule: "(2) Mercury for education." Chart 2 applies it immediately: "In this chart Mercury, signifying education, is posited in Aquarius…"
Effect of the rule: Level, subject and breaks in education are read from Mercury.
Combination of the rule: Learning, studies, qualification are to be read.

Rule description: Saturn is the karaka for profession
Exact rule: "(3) Saturn for profession."
Effect of the rule: The kind of work, and every change of it, is read from Saturn.
Combination of the rule: Occupation, work, service or business is to be read.

Rule description: Venus is the karaka for marriage
Exact rule: "(4) Venus for marriages."
Effect of the rule: Fact, timing and quality of marriage are read from Venus.

Rule description: Jupiter over Ketu's sign gives pilgrimage
Exact rule: "(5) Jupiter's transit over the sign occupied by Ketu for religious travels or pilgrimages."
Effect of the rule: Religious travel, pilgrimage, and by extension the turn towards renunciation.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter in transit reaches the sign occupied at birth by Ketu.

Rule description: The Sun is the karaka for the father
Exact rule: "The Master answers that as the Sun representing father is posited in Virgo…" — the entire paternal reading of Chart 1 is built from the Sun outward, using exactly the procedure of RAO-FND-009: the sign the Sun occupies, the planet with him, and the 2nd house to the Sun.
Effect of the rule: Father's profession, income and landholding.
Combination of the rule: The father's occupation, wealth and property are to be read.

Rule description: The Moon is the karaka for the mother and the elder sister
Exact rule: In Chart 1 the Moon in the sign previous to Jupiter's yields "he has an elder sister"; later, "The Moon representing elder sister is in the 12th to Jupiter's placement at birth" and her death is read from the Moon's contacts. In the same chart the Moon beside Ketu in Capricorn/Sagittarius is read as Parvati — the mother-goddess — in the name-derivation.
Effect of the rule: Elder sisters are counted backwards from Jupiter; the mother is read from the Moon's sign and company.
Combination of the rule: Female elders and elder siblings are to be read.

Rule description: Jupiter also stands for the native himself, and for the soul
Exact rule: "Jupiter represents the native" (printed p. 11) and "Jupiter who represents the soul" (printed p. 13). Jupiter is therefore simultaneously (a) the significator of the native's own person, (b) the karaka of children, and (c) the moving hand of the clock.
Effect of the rule: Wherever the reading concerns the native as such — his rise, his fame, his death — Jupiter is the reference planet.

Rule description: Saturn is neither good nor bad
Exact rule: "Saturn is the Lord of Karma (work). He is neither good nor bad. The results depend on the position of Saturn."
Effect of the rule: Saturn's verdict is wholly positional. Same planet, different sign, opposite result.

Rule description: The six things that decide a planet's result
Exact rule: Verbatim, the complete list: "When considering results the sign occupied by a planet, the Lord of the sign, the other planets posited in that sign, the planets in the 7th and 12th to the planet, whose effects are being considered, have to be taken into account for assessing the results. The exchange of signs of that planet with another is also taken into consideration. In addition the transit of Jupiter is taken into account."
Effect of the rule: Seven inputs, in the author's order — (1) the sign the planet occupies; (2) the lord of that sign; (3) other planets in that same sign (conjunction); (4) planets in the 7th from it (opposition); (5) planets in the 12th from it; (6) exchange of signs (parivartana) with another planet; (7) the transit of Jupiter. DERIVED — reconciling this with RAO-FND-009. The Introduction's step-by-step instruction says "the adjacent houses of that planet and the seventh house therefrom" — i.e. the 12th, the 2nd, and the 7th. This list names the 12th and the 7th but not the 2nd. The casebook settles it: the 2nd house from a planet is used constantly — Chart 1, "Saturn in the 2nd house to the Sun … indicates one owning some lands" and "The placement of Mercury and Saturn in the 2nd to the Sun indicates sources of income"; Chart 2, "the placement of Mars and Venus in the 2nd house to Saturn." Use all four: 12th, own sign, 2nd, 7th.
Combination of the rule: The result of any planet is being assessed.

Rule description: Jupiter's transit gives the results of the sign he stands in
Exact rule: "In addition the transit of Jupiter is taken into account. He gives the results of the sign he transits."
Effect of the rule: Whatever the sign and its occupants promise fires in the year Jupiter arrives there.

Rule description: "Contact" is the operative verb
Exact rule: DERIVED from consistent usage. The book says Jupiter "contacts" Mars, Rahu, Venus, the Sun, Saturn, the Moon. In every instance this means transiting Jupiter enters the sign in which that planet stands at birth — it is a whole-sign conjunction by transit, not an aspect and not a degree-based conjunction.
Effect of the rule: At contact, the contacted planet's karakatwa is delivered — for good or ill according to its condition.
Combination of the rule: Transiting Jupiter arrives at a sign occupied by a natal planet.

Rule description: Saturn does the work; Jupiter enjoys the fruit
Exact rule: The disciple raises exactly this objection — "why here importance is given to Jupiter which is not the case usually as the question of livelihood is considered from Saturn's movements in most of the cases." The Master answers: "while work done is the result of Saturn, the enjoyment of the result is ascribed to Jupiter who represents the soul."
Effect of the rule: Ask "what work?" of Saturn. Ask "when does it pay, and how well?" of Jupiter.
Combination of the rule: Livelihood is being timed, and the reader asks why Jupiter is used when profession belongs to Saturn.

Rule description: Transmission: a planet passes Jupiter's touch onward
Exact rule: Verbatim mechanism: "The transit of Jupiter on the Sun and Venus was transmitted by them to Saturn placed in the 2nd house to them (owned by Venus also) and this leads to vitalizing Saturn conjunct Mercury which shapes the life by offering a high post in a Government Engineering College."
Effect of the rule: Jupiter's contact does not stop at the planet he meets: it flows into the next sign's occupants and vitalises them. Chains of two are worked in the book; longer chains are not.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter in transit contacts planet A; planet B stands in the 2nd house to A.

Rule description: A planet in the previous sign to another
Exact rule: "Here, Jupiter is in Capricorn all alone. There is the Moon in the previous sign to the one occupied by Jupiter. Hence, he has an elder sister."
Effect of the rule: Behind the karaka = elder. Ahead of the karaka = younger. Because Jupiter moves forward, what he has already passed is senior and what he has yet to reach is junior.
Combination of the rule: A planet stands in the sign immediately before the karaka.

Rule description: Aspect is a weaker relation than contact
Exact rule: "In the first round of 12 years, Jupiter, when he enters Pisces, has the aspects of retrograde Mars in Aries, and so the native will suffer from wounds and swelling on account of pollution of blood." And later: "When in the 4th round Jupiter transits his own house Pisces, he gets the aspect of Venus from Virgo conjunct the Sun, the native will get into possession of parental property."
Effect of the rule: DERIVED — the aspect used. Pisces ← Virgo is the 7th; Pisces ← Aries is the 12th/2nd adjacency. Both fall inside the frame already given by RAO-FND-009 and RAO-FND-019. Read "aspect" as the 7th-house opposition, and adjacency as its own separate relation.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter in transit stands where another planet aspects him.

Rule description: Younger brothers are counted by Jupiter's first round
Exact rule: The worked census, verbatim: "Jupiter represents the native, and in his transits he crosses (1) Mars, (2) Rahu, (3) the Sun, (4) Saturn and (5) Mercury. So he will have five younger brothers and as there is Venus over which Jupiter transits in his first round, he will have one younger sister."
Effect of the rule: DERIVED — the sex convention this implies. Jupiter natal in Capricorn crosses, going forward: Aquarius(–), Pisces(–), Aries Mars, Taurus(–), Gemini Rahu, Cancer(–), Leo(–), Virgo Sun + Venus, Libra Saturn + Mercury, Scorpio(–), Sagittarius Moon + Ketu. Counting the masculine and neuter bodies gives Mars, Rahu, Sun, Saturn, Mercury = five younger brothers; the feminine body Venus gives one younger sister. The Moon, in the sign behind Jupiter, was already spent on the elder sister (RAO-FND-024) and is not counted again. Ketu is not counted at all. Working convention therefore: Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, Rahu → brothers; Moon, Venus → sisters; Ketu → not a sibling.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter's natal sign is fixed; the planets he will cross in his first round are listed in order.

Rule description: Reading community and name from the planetary tableau
Exact rule: The Master's reading, part by part: Jupiter in a Saturn-owned sign = Iswara (Shiva); the Moon below him = Parvati; Ketu = the tail; Rahu = the mouth; Mars = the horns; Jupiter = the stomach. Moon with Ketu in one sign = "Kshiramsa Sambhuta", one born of the Ocean of Milk (Parvati).
Effect of the rule: The assembled figure is a Nandi (bull) — so the native is a Saivite, and his name is likely to be Shiva's vehicle: Nandi, Vrishabha, Basava, or a name carrying those letters at its beginning or end. The native "does not see any difference between Shiva and Hari."
Combination of the rule: Jupiter in Capricorn (a Saturn sign, called Iswaramsa), with the Moon and Ketu in the sign just below, Rahu elsewhere, Mars in Aries.

Rule description: The father: Sun in a sign of vegetation, with Venus
Exact rule: Each clause is read separately and then summed — the exact procedure of RAO-FND-009.
Effect of the rule: Father is an agriculturist (Sun in Virgo); he amassed money through his profession (Sun conjunct Venus); he owns lands (Saturn 2nd to the Sun, aspected by Mars) — but "it was not much as Venus was weak" (Venus debilitated); his income was meagre because Mercury and Saturn in the 2nd are opposed by strong enemy Mars; and he spent lavishly, "the Sun is conjunct Venus who is vain-glorious and so wants a royal type of living." And the strange verdict: this money "will be distributed to the other brothers of the native and the parents' own brothers."
Combination of the rule: Sun in Virgo ("a sign of vegetation, good crops etc."), conjunct Venus; Saturn in the 2nd to the Sun (Libra), aspected directly by Mars; Venus debilitated and weak in Virgo; Mercury also in the 2nd to the Sun, both opposed by a strong Mars who is an enemy.

Rule description: Profession from the company Mercury and Saturn keep
Exact rule: Three karakatwas are laid side by side: Venus (whose house it is) "stands for Arts"; Mars "stands for Engineering and Machinery"; Mercury is education and Saturn is profession.
Effect of the rule: "one has to infer that the native may take up a profession in Engineering and work in an educational institution." Fulfilled later as "a high post in a Government Engineering College" and "employed in a Government Institution in a gazetted rank" (Jupiter contacting exalted Saturn in Libra).
Combination of the rule: Saturn conjunct Mercury in Libra (the house of Venus), both aspected by Mars.

Rule description: Death of the elder sister, and the retrograde signature
Exact rule: The Nandi Nadi records this at sloka 5 under the mathematical symbol 3 4 4 5 — "the native will have break in his studies at 17 and incur heavy expenses, and the elder sister of the native will pass away at that time." The Master then derives the same result: in the second round, Jupiter contacts Mars (3rd from the Moon) while both are aspected by Mercury (4th), giving heavy expenses; then Jupiter contacts Rahu at 17–18.
Effect of the rule: Break in studies, heavy expenses, and the death of the elder sister. Retrogression is a malefic amplifier — "Rahu (a retrograde planet) … causing many troubles and miseries" and "Rahu, who is always retrograde."
Combination of the rule: The Moon (elder sister) stands 12th to natal Jupiter; in transit the Moon's significator-chain contacts retrograde Mars and Rahu, "who is always retrograde."

Rule description: Exchange of signs saves the child
Exact rule: This is item (6) of RAO-FND-019 in action.
Effect of the rule: "both having exchange of places, the child will escape drowning."
Combination of the rule: Mercury in Libra and Venus in Virgo — each in the other's sign, a clean exchange (parivartana); Jupiter transits both in the first round.

Rule description: Foreign travel from Rahu, the Moon and exalted Jupiter
Exact rule: Rahu supplies the going-abroad; the Moon in the 7th supplies the crossing of water; Jupiter's own exaltation in the next sign sustains it.
Effect of the rule: Foreign travel; then, "when Jupiter contacts the Sun in Virgo, the native will get a higher job on return from foreign travels, and higher emoluments" — Virgo, 4th round, age 44.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter in transit conjoins Rahu in Gemini and thereby "gets the aspect of the Moon in Sagittarius" (the 7th); the very next sign, Cancer, is Jupiter's exaltation and is owned by that same Moon.

Rule description: Fame at the completion of a round
Exact rule: "Jupiter, when completing the 3rd round, will have travelled for 36 years and offers name and fame to the native at that age of transiting his natal position."
Effect of the rule: Name, fame and the consolidation of status. In this chart 36 also gives a son (RAO-FND-010), and 48 closes the fourth round with status still rising "until Jupiter reaches Pisces" at 50.
Combination of the rule: Transiting Jupiter returns to his own natal sign, completing a round.

Rule description: Death timed by Jupiter's contact with Rahu
Exact rule: "We now come to the last chapter of this life story when Jupiter contacts Rahu in his 5th round. This will be when the native will attain the age of 53. This transit will cause death of the native."
Effect of the rule: Death of the native. > GUARDRAIL — LONGEVITY AND DEATH. This rule and every death-timing rule in this corpus is > catalogued as classical source material, not endorsed and not to be delivered as a finding > about any living person. Rao's own text warns, of married life, that "great care should be > taken in making such predictions" (Chart 2, printed p. 14). Predicted death-dates cause real > harm and the arithmetic above is, on the book's own showing, ambiguous. Never tell anyone when > they or a relative will die.
Combination of the rule: Transiting Jupiter contacts Rahu in the 5th round.

Rule description: A GOOD ASTROLOGER NEVER DWELLS ON THE SINISTER
Exact rule: The author states the rule of practice himself, in his own voice, and it is the most important single sentence in the corpus for anyone using it on a living person: > "The results of the combination of Rahu-Mars and Venus-Jupiter in the next has been detailed in > several horoscopes already dealt with. It is always better to stop after discussing a good > indication by the combination … since a good astrologer should never dwell on those points."
Effect of the rule: The operational rule: name the favourable, stop at the sinister. The harsh verdicts throughout RULES-DOM, RULES-HLT and RULES-PBR are catalogued so the book is honestly represented — and this rule is the author's own authority for never delivering them. Compare his warning at Chart 2: "great care should be taken in making such predictions."
Combination of the rule: A reading has produced both favourable and sinister indications.

Rule description: The controlled comparison: two similar charts, and the discriminating factor
Exact rule: The Master's own procedure for the problem RAO-JTC-014 poses. Having read Chart 139, he volunteers a second nativity "born 3 years and 8 months before" the first — Mars, Sun and Mercury in Pisces, Venus in Aries, Ketu in Taurus, Jupiter in Gemini, Saturn in Cancer, Rahu in Scorpio — and then states the difference: > "There is so much similarity; but Mars was weak too and so was the Sun — both fiery planets in > a watery sign. Hence, there was no aggressiveness in that case."
Effect of the rule: In the same chart Rao states the negative form of the same rule outright: "Simply because Mars is in Leo and Venus is in Virgo, you cannot predict the same thing in all cases. This is a peculiar case."
Combination of the rule: Two charts carry closely similar configurations but produce different results.

Rule description: The what-if reading: an alternative chart offered for an uncertain Moon
Exact rule: Rao writes both readings and lets the reader choose, which is exactly what a practitioner facing an uncertain birth time must do: - Ch 115 — "This is a very ordinary horoscope. If, however, the Moon be placed in Saturn's house at birth, Saturn and the Moon will get exchange of places… This position of the Moon will give the native a better position in life. Otherwise it will be of a very devotional aptitude." - Ch 130 — "If the Moon be in any of the 4 places from Sagittarius to Pisces, the native will be a thrifty person…" - Ch 119 — an alternative for the birthplace: "the native would have been born near a church or a female deity's temple. Otherwise he would have been born in a maternity centre."
Effect of the rule: Two readings, each conditional on the disputed placement.
Combination of the rule: A fast-moving body — in practice the Moon — cannot be pinned to a sign (RAO-FND-002, RAO-FND-005).

Rule description: The planets are read as a royal court, with motives
Exact rule: The corpus's readings are dramatic, not mechanical — the planets have offices and motives, and the verdict is the story they enact. The roles are stable across the book: | Body | Role at court | |---|---| | Sun | The King; his own sign is his "Headquarters" (RAO-KRK-065) — Ch 139, "the Sun in Scorpio is on duty at his machinery headquarters" | | Jupiter | The Master, holding "Chief Minister's post" — Ch 139, Ch 143 | | Mars | The Commander-in-Chief — Ch 143 | | Rahu | The doorkeeper, and a mouth that swallows — Ch 73, Ch 143 ("Saturn to enter Rahu's mouth") | | Venus | The treasure being guarded — Ch 143
Effect of the rule: A narrative reading in which planetary strength is the characters' capacity to act.

Rule description: "THESE MATTERS SHOULD NEVER BE REVEALED"
Exact rule: Having just proved a general rule from three comparative charts (RAO-FND-040), the Master immediately forbids its use, in the plainest words in the book: > "…it may be concluded that when Jupiter has no planet either in the adjacent houses or in the > 7th house, the native of such a horoscope will be short-lived. If Saturn is similarly disposed, > the native of such a horoscope will experience poverty and difficulties in life. > These matters should never be revealed, and the revealer will suffer extreme difficulties."
Effect of the rule: Operational rule for this whole track: longevity and destitution verdicts are extracted for scholarly completeness and are never delivered. This is why RAO-FND-034 carries an absolute guardrail, and why RAO-HLT-013 is operationally disabled.
Combination of the rule: A reading has produced a short-life or a poverty verdict.

Rule description: The corpus proves a rule by comparing three charts
Exact rule: The Master announces the procedure, executes it, and states the conclusion — the only fully worked induction in the book: > "I shall describe three horoscopes in support of my contention." Three charts follow, each with Jupiter unsupported in a different way — hemmed by Rahu in Aquarius; debilitated and facing an enemy in his own exaltation sign; debilitated in Capricorn with empty adjacencies and "strong Rahu … meets weak Jupiter and gobbles him up." Then: > "Therefore, in view of the examples described above, it may be concluded that…"
Effect of the rule: A general rule — which the very next sentence forbids anyone to use (RAO-FND-039).
Combination of the rule: A general principle is to be established rather than a single chart read.

Rule description: The corpus names its sources and its interlocutors
Exact rule: Three attributions appear in this block, and they matter for RAO-FND-006, which said only that the book draws "some portions from Nandi Nadi and some from Bhrigu Nadi": - Ch 243 — after a full reading ending in a death dated to a Tuesday: "This is an analysis of a horoscope from Bhrigu Samhita." - Ch 250 — "The native will have two sons and a greater number of daughters according to Atmarishi's opinion." — a named rishi cited for a disputed point. - Ch 282 — the disciple is addressed by name: "Preceptor: Oh Manu, we shall discuss this horoscope in detail." Elsewhere the pair are Nandikeswara and Markandeya (Chart 1); here the frame changes.
Effect of the rule: Provenance for individual verdicts.

Rule description: The same chart yields a second, alternative profession
Exact rule: Rao does this often enough to be a habit, and he announces it: - Ch 270 — "Another kind of profession is also predicted for this kind of horoscope." — followed by a completely separate derivation ending in forest-products and ornament-making. - Ch 243 — "Analysing in a different manner, it can be stated that Venus indicates beauty, Mercury indicates writing … and Rahu indicates dark colour. Therefore, the native's father will do some business or work related to these things." - Ch 253 — the male reading is completed, then: "Disciple: Master, what will be the fortunes of a woman with this kind of planetary combination?" (RAO-DOM-038).
Effect of the rule: Two or more readings of one chart, held side by side.
Combination of the rule: A chart has been read once; the Master reads it again by another route.

Rule description: "THIS IS HOW THE PREDICTION IS MADE"
Exact rule: The most valuable methodological passage in the book. The Master answers in four moves, and then names what he has just done: > "When we say intellect, it is a combination of brain and power. It is stone and earth together > that constitute a house. Similarly, when there is combination of Mercury and Mars, having Venus > in the second or the seventh to them — or when Venus is conjunct Mars — it is generally found that > the native will come to own a house or will have landed property. But, in the present case, > Mars goes to his house of debilitation and has Rahu in fourth with no planets in between. Hence, > the prediction 'old house, with a well in it'. As Rahu always moves backwards, the house is about > to tumble down. Venus conjunct Mars with Cancer vacant shows water facilities. This is how the > prediction is made."
Effect of the rule: This is why RAO-JTC-014 is true and unavoidable. The general rule is stable; the modifiers are what differ between charts, and they are what turn one rule into a hundred different verdicts. A reading that reports the general rule without its modifiers has not made a prediction — it has quoted a lookup table.
Combination of the rule: The disciple asks not what the verdict is but how it was reached.

Rule description: "To estimate the age is a tough job"
Exact rule: The Master does not claim precision he has not got: > "The disciple wanted to know how the age of the native is fixed for the several events > happening in life. The Master answered — To estimate the age is a tough job. Any way, reckoning > from the transits of Jupiter, we find Jupiter transits the sign occupied by the Moon at birth > (viz. Gemini) about the 19th year of the native or about 20."
Effect of the rule: Ages are estimates from Jupiter's transits, stated as windows.
Combination of the rule: The disciple asks how the ages of events are fixed.

Rule description: Matching a chart to a known chart transfers its verdict
Exact rule: RAO-FND-036 and RAO-FND-040 used two or three charts to establish a rule; here the comparison is used to transfer a verdict directly: > "Preceptor: I shall narrate a horoscope of a person born earlier by four years, eight months > and nine days. … Due to these combinations, the native was destined to marry a widow. Now, > coming to the present horoscope, we have to say that this native will also marry a widow." And bluntly, at Chart 314: "The native of this horoscope will also live the same kind of life as the one of 313."
Effect of the rule: A verdict carried across from a known chart.
Combination of the rule: A chart closely resembles one already read.

Rule description: The closing section USES the Lagna, the dasa and the nakshatra
Exact rule: Two of this corpus's founding axioms are set aside by the author himself at the end of his own book. RAO-FND-001 says the Lagna is not primary; RAO-FND-004 says dasa is not the timing engine — and Rao's objection to dasa was stated in the Introduction in his own voice. Yet the closing readings run on Vimshottari dasa, from a nakshatra, with an Ascendant: > "…and the Ascendant, being Virgo, the native of this horoscope would be born in a street > running East to West." > "The native was born under the asterism of Krittika, third quarter. The relevant Solar Dasha > (period) was for a period of two years. … On completion of his second year the Moon's Dasha > would commence. … From his 12th year, Mars Dasha would commence affecting his fortunes for a > period of seven years. … From his 19th year, the period of the Dragon's head would commence. > This is a Dasha of 18 years." > "The native was born under the 2nd quarter of the asterism of Jyeshtha. The relevant Budha > Dasha had expired upto a little in Chandra's Bhukthi. … the balance in Budha Dasha at the time > of birth was 9 years and 6 months."
Effect of the rule: Operational rule: tag the provenance. A BNN engine built on this corpus must not silently mix the Jupiter-transit clock with Vimshottari. They are two systems bound into one volume.
Combination of the rule: Any rule drawn from the closing pages.

Rule description: The nakshatra-pada refinement answers the Introduction's own problem
Exact rule: The Introduction opened the book with this problem (RAO-FND-003) — that a few hours can reverse a verdict. The book closes by solving it, with padas and longitudes: > "When two charts are examined, the natives being born at an interval of 5 days as in (A1) and > (B1), if we know the exact positions (longitudes) then a correct judgement of effects in life > can be given." Four graded cases follow, distinguished only by pada: | Case | Configuration | Verdict | |---|---|---| | (i) | Sun in Ashwini 1st, Venus Ashwini 1st, Mercury Bharani 1st — all in first quarters | "a case of Yoga Bhanga = misfortunes" | | (ii) | Venus Ashwini 1st, Sun Ashwini 3rd, Mercury Bharani 3rd, Venus just behind the Sun | "least fruitful" | | (iii) | Venus Ashwini 1st, Sun Bharani 4th, Mercury Krittika | "mediocre fortune" | | (iv) | Venus Ashwini 1st, Mercury Ashwini 4th, Sun Bharani 1st | "gives good results" | And the governing principle: "The results depend on whether the planets are friendly or inimical. Harmonious results prevail when friendly planets are placed either together or in adjoining signs."
Effect of the rule: Two near-identical charts separated, and graded.
Combination of the rule: Two people born days apart, whose whole-sign charts are indistinguishable.

Rule description: Palmistry: the author cites his own book, and the question is closed
Exact rule: After nine scattered instances across the corpus, the closing pages make the position explicit — Rao refers the reader to a separate book of his own: > "For further elucidation with reference to the lines on the palm, see the author's book 'Natal > Chart From Palm' — available with M/s Ranjan Publications, 16, Ansari Road, New Delhi-2." And the closing charts are saturated with it, several opening with the palm before the chart: - Ch 418 — "will have a Vishnu line in his hand … the sign of Pisces and a star also in his palm" - Ch 419 — "Nandikeswara informs Markandeya that the native will have Vishnu line as well as Mani-malika in his palm" - Ch 425 — "a big serpent sign on his palm as well as a trident, the weapon of Lord Subramanya" - Ch 426 — "the fate line having a full blown lotus sign by its side, lifeline touching Venus line with a fish sign also. His chart is given here." - Ch 434 — "His right palm shows an unblemished long life line and a trident" - Ch 421 — Rao's own exclamation: "The life-line in the palm is thick and broken. What a clear harmony between the science of Astrology and Palmistry!"
Effect of the rule: Verdicts the horoscope alone does not supply.
Combination of the rule: Method — the palmistry layer, finally settled

Rule description: Vastu Hara: reading a place with no chart at all
Exact rule: A short section, unlike anything else in the book, in which the Master reads people and households purely from the ground they stand on: > "Heaven's Rays on human houses — Vastu Hara. (Taken from old Shastraic texts on House > Construction etc.) From the Master's observations on the entrances to the town or village and > the various residential quarters, all about the places and people living in the houses is > described with some illustrations. For the gaining of worldly knowledge the Master and disciple > have started on the first journey to visit holy places and rivers." Eight numbered observations follow — on entering a village, "This place is one where people are wedded to Dharma, and rich and well educated"; to a shopkeeper, "You cannot gain by this trade … You will have to migrate"; to a householder, "You have been suffering a great deal for the last 6 months … Things will be alright six months hence."
Effect of the rule: A reading of a place and its inhabitants without any horoscope.
Combination of the rule: No horoscope; only a village, a street or a house.

Rule description: Mundane prediction from an individual chart
Exact rule: The only mundane passage in the book, and it is prompted by exactly the right question: > "The disciple wanted to know how an individual's chart could indicate the fate of the > country. The Master answers: When Jupiter transits Cancer and Saturn, Rahu combine in Leo with > the Sun, Mercury in Cancer or Leo and with Mars in Gemini or Cancer, and during this critical > period the Moon crosses Capricorn and Aquarius, the northern part of the country will face > great flood havoc … in the southern region there will be quarrels … in another part there > will be explosions … poisonous gases causing death on a large scale. The Time Lord (Kala > Purusha), Rahu, having occupied the fiery sign Leo all alone with Saturn in the 12th > (Poisons), moves around…"
Effect of the rule: Floods, civil conflict, explosions — mundane events, dated by transit.
Combination of the rule: The disciple asks how one person's chart can show the fate of a country.

Rule description: "Wind trouble" is the corpus's default affliction
Exact rule: By far the most frequently named complaint in the book: - Ch 1 — "the child will suffer from windy troubles in his 6th year when Jupiter transits Gemini where Rahu is posited." - Ch 15 — "Saturn-Rahu conjunction indicates wind troubles to the parents." - Ch 50 — "The placement of Rahu next to Jupiter indicates wind troubles and nervous weakness." - Ch 33 — Saturn, Jupiter and Rahu in Virgo: "the native's physical body is windy in temperament." - Ch 42 — "He will suffer from piles and wind troubles" on retirement at 56–57.
Effect of the rule: Wind disorders, nervous weakness, piles.
Combination of the rule: Saturn with Rahu, or Rahu adjacent to Jupiter, or Saturn/Rahu prominent in the frame.

Rule description: Phlegm from the Moon and Saturn
Exact rule: "The transit indicates phlegmatic and windy troubles for the mother (the Moon) as well as the native (Jupiter)." Ch 48 gives the same complaint plainly: "He will suffer from colds."
Effect of the rule: Colds, phlegm, chest complaints.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter in transit conjoining the Moon and Saturn together.

Rule description: Mars gives wounds, blood and heat
Exact rule: "Jupiter, when he enters Pisces, has the aspects of retrograde Mars in Aries, and so the native will suffer from wounds and swelling on account of pollution of blood."
Effect of the rule: Wounds, swellings, blood disorders.
Combination of the rule: Retrograde Mars aspecting the sign Jupiter transits.

Exact rule: "The native will be afraid of serpents as Jupiter transits Rahu. Being placed in his own house Jupiter provides necessary removal of fear."
Effect of the rule: Fear arising, and relieved.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter transits Rahu, Jupiter being placed in his own house.

Rule description: Build and colour from Jupiter's dignity
Exact rule: Exalted Jupiter — Ch 9, "Jupiter is exalted in this case and so the native has a well-proportioned body with golden colour." - Ch 34 — "He will have a lean body." - Ch 1 — "the native … has a lean body." - Ch 29 — "The native will have corpulent body and will be of sportive nature."
Effect of the rule: Build, proportion and complexion.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter's dignity is noted; Jupiter is the native (RAO-KRK-001).

Rule description: Satwic, Rajasic, Tamasic — the mind's grade
Exact rule: "As Jupiter has Saturn in 7th from his placement the native is good minded, and Satwic in nature (as opposed to Rajasic and Tamasic)." The same axis in Ch 20 gives "an Iswaramsa Sambhuta … one wedded to both Dharma (moral principle: Jupiter) and Karma (action: Saturn)."
Effect of the rule: A satwic, dharmic temperament.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter with Saturn in the 7th from him.

Rule description: An unstable mind from Venus in the Moon's sign
Exact rule: Ch 32 — "Venus is placed in the Moon's house causing an unstable mind and unhappiness." - Ch 28 — "The native will have no peace of mind as the Moon in Libra has Rahu after him in Sagittarius." - Ch 6 — a previous-birth curse gives "little income and a perturbed mind."
Effect of the rule: Restlessness, instability, want of peace.
Combination of the rule: The Moon, or Cancer — "the house of mind" (RAO-KRK-012) — is afflicted.

Rule description: Operations, and the ages they fall at
Exact rule: Surgery is stated flatly and dated, without the mechanism always being named: - Ch 65 — "Between 52-54, he will undergo an operation and thereafter improve his health." - Ch 80 — "He will have an operation at 35-36." - Ch 77 — "the mother will suffer from stomach trouble as the Moon is placed in the house adjoining Rahu. Rule description: The Moon afflicted by Rahu, Venus and Mars: disturbance of mind
Exact rule: "As the Moon is opposed by Venus and Rahu, Mars occupying the precedent house, the native will have mental aberrations and he will be possessed by spirits, which happens in the 17th, 19th and 20th years." Ch 65 gives "in his 43rd, 47th and 53rd year he will have mind troubles."
