Rule description: The corpus contains one attempted suicide, and it is averted
Exact rule: "…the native will get disturbed in mind and will then try to commit suicide by taking poison. Venus being conjunct Ketu (who moves backwards) saves the native. This happens between 18th and 20th years, or 23rd year."
Effect of the rule: (This rule is catalogued for corpus completeness and is operationally disabled.)
Combination of the rule: Saturn aspecting Venus; Jupiter and Saturn aspected by Mars; Jupiter opposed by Venus and Ketu and so "finds it difficult to help."

Rule description: Weak constitution as an impediment in its own right
Exact rule: "Ketu in the 2nd house to Jupiter indicates nervous weakness … His weak constitution will act as an impediment. The 12th, 24th and 37th years are full of troubles." Ch 98: "during the 5th year the boy will suffer from stomach trouble, colds and nervous debility."
Effect of the rule: A frail constitution limiting what the rest of the chart promises.
Combination of the rule: Ketu in the 2nd house to Jupiter; the Moon in Anishtamsa, conjunct Rahu.

Rule description: The corpus gives dietary advice, not only ritual
Exact rule: The one place in the corpus where the advice is purely dietary and medical, with no ritual attached at all: > "As Mars and Ketu are stationed behind Jupiter, the native will be afflicted by piles. The > liver complaints will be the cause of piles, and the native will have to avoid taking such food > as will disorder the stomach. The native should take green vegetables in plenty." Chart 379 likewise sends the native to a doctor: at 27 "he will have an accident but will escape serious consequences by the help of doctors."
Effect of the rule: Dietary and medical management of a named complaint.
Combination of the rule: Mars and Ketu behind Jupiter, giving piles with a liver cause.

Rule description: The arithmetic of the clock
Exact rule: DERIVED, and verified to the year. Jupiter walks forward one sign per year from his natal sign. Let k = number of signs from natal Jupiter to the target sign, counting the natal sign as 0. Then > age = k + 12 × (round − 1) Round 1 = ages 0–11, round 2 = 12–23, round 3 = 24–35, round 4 = 36–47, round 5 = 48–59.
Effect of the rule: Verified against Chart 1 at six independent points: Jupiter natal Capricorn — Gemini (Rahu) round 1 = 6 ✓ "windy troubles in his 6th year"; Virgo/Libra round 1 = 8–9 ✓ "9th and 10th years … escape drowning"; Gemini round 2 = 17 ✓ "at the age of 17-18"; natal return round 3 = 36 ✓ "will have travelled for 36 years"; Gemini round 4 = 41 ✓ "about the years 41-42"; Gemini round 5 = 53 ✓ "attain the age of 53."

Rule description: Contact: the definition of a hit
Exact rule: "Contacts" means whole-sign arrival — not degree conjunction, not aspect.
Effect of the rule: The natal planet's karakatwa is delivered, coloured by its condition and its company.
Combination of the rule: A transiting planet enters the sign a natal planet occupies.

Rule description: The completed round gives name and fame
Exact rule: Marked in its own right, independent of the sign's occupants.
Effect of the rule: Name, fame, consolidation of status.
Combination of the rule: Transiting Jupiter returns to his natal sign.

Rule description: Jupiter contacting his enemies spoils the matter he rules
Exact rule: "He will have only medium education as Jupiter contacts his enemies Mercury, Venus and Ketu around his 12th year."
Effect of the rule: Education capped at medium.
Combination of the rule: In his first round, Jupiter contacts planets that are his enemies — here Mercury, Venus and Ketu — before the round closes.

Rule description: Named transit windows for named matters
Exact rule: "When transiting Leo, Libra and Scorpio, Jupiter will provide occasions for marriages etc., and the native will own a house."
Effect of the rule: Marriages in the family, and acquisition of a house.

Rule description: "Contacts A first, then B" fixes the ORDER of life events
Exact rule: This is the second great mechanism of the book after the karaka rule, and it is used on every page. The karaka's itinerary is the native's life story, in order. Worked instances: - Chart 9 — "As Saturn contacts Venus and Mercury first and then the Sun, Mars and Rahu, he will be a money lender and dealer in jewellery." - Chart 11 — "As Saturn contacts Rahu first and Mars next, the native will take up wood sawing as his profession." - Chart 6 — "Saturn contacts Rahu at first, then Venus and the Moon who exchange places with Mercury — hence, he deals in drinks and dresses and will carry on business in various places." - Chart 21 — "He will start with writing until the influence of Mars and Ketu is over and when Saturn contacts Venus in his own house, he will come into lime light. As Saturn contacts Mercury and the Sun in the next house, the native will enter into a treasury section." - Chart 8 — "As Jupiter transits Mars first and Saturn next, the native will have two brothers younger to him."
Effect of the rule: The sequence of professions, gains and losses across a life — and, for Jupiter, the birth order of siblings (RAO-FND-026).
Combination of the rule: A karaka is set walking forward from its natal sign; the natal planets it will meet are listed in the order it meets them.

Rule description: A karaka's itinerary names the profession by blending what it meets
Exact rule: The planets met are read as a compound, not one at a time. Worked: - Chart 11 — Saturn meets Rahu then Mars: "(Rahu, Mars indicate dry wood and the Sun-Venus conjunct, Mercury next indicate a clever way of giving new shape to the dry forest wood products)" → wood sawing / timber. - Chart 9 — Saturn meets Venus + Mercury, then Sun, Mars, Rahu → money lending and jewellery (Venus = valuables, Mercury = accounting, Mars/Rahu = the hard edge of lending). - Chart 3 — the Sun (father) walking forward meets Mars + Rahu, then Saturn + Moon → "he will earn livelihood through machinery and judiciary (settlement of disputes between the employees and employers owning Machinery)."
Effect of the rule: A named trade, compounded from the karakatwas met in order.
Combination of the rule: Saturn (or the Sun, for the father) walks forward and meets a run of planets.

Rule description: Saturn's transit times the change of work
Exact rule: "His transit indicates the changes." Saturn spends ≈2½ years per sign, ≈30 years per round.
Effect of the rule: Changes of work, and afflictions to whatever the transited planets signify.
Combination of the rule: Saturn transits a sign holding natal planets.

Rule description: Mars's transit order times the fate of brothers
Exact rule: "His elder brother passed away early in life (Mars in transit comes across Rahu first)."
Effect of the rule: Meeting Rahu first ruins the matter Mars carries.
Combination of the rule: Mars set walking forward from his natal sign; the first natal planet he meets is noted.

Rule description: Venus's transit clock, counted from an event
Exact rule: "Venus transits Cancer in the 3rd year and Virgo in the 5th year after elopement — these are hard times for the native's wife as Venus is conjunct Rahu in Virgo."
Effect of the rule: Hard times while Venus stands with Rahu; relief when Jupiter reaches Leo.
Combination of the rule: Venus walks forward after a dated event.

Rule description: Both clocks confirming is the strongest reading
Exact rule: DERIVED from the book's habit. Rao's most confident statements are the ones where a transit and a natal disposition point the same way — Chart 25's "Saturn transits Virgo and is aspected by Jupiter in Pisces at birth"; Chart 1's Jupiter contacting exalted natal Saturn in Libra for the gazetted post.
Effect of the rule: A firm verdict rather than a likelihood.
Combination of the rule: A transiting planet arrives where a natal planet also aspects or occupies.

Rule description: Retrogression amplifies the malefic
Exact rule: "Jupiter contacts Rahu (a retrograde planet) at the age of 17-18 and causing many troubles and miseries"; "Rahu, who is always retrograde"; "retrograde Mars in Aries and so the native will suffer from wounds and swelling."
Effect of the rule: Trouble, misery, wounds — the planet's harsher face.
Combination of the rule: The contacted planet is retrograde; Rahu and Ketu are always retrograde.

Rule description: Rahu moves backward, and so "pounces" on what lies behind him
Exact rule: "Here, Rahu is about to pounce upon Venus. This indicates a widow." Chart 10 has Rahu in Capricorn and Venus in Sagittarius — Rahu, moving backwards, is about to arrive on Venus.
Effect of the rule: What lies behind Rahu is what he is about to spoil.
Combination of the rule: Rahu stands in the sign after a planet.

Rule description: The same contact does not give the same result twice
Exact rule: The disciple asks the exact question a rule-extractor must ask — "Are we to take it that in every case where the Moon is conjunct a malefic, and there is Parivartana of that planet with another, there is likely to be a bad history behind the mother?" The Master's answer, verbatim: "So, we cannot have the same results always. The particular place of conjunction, the planet involved and other influences based on Karakatwa have to be taken into consideration to come to proper conclusion. One must be extremely careful in arriving at conclusions by taking a comprehensive approach."
Effect of the rule: Corroborating evidence: in Chart 1 the single contact Jupiter → Rahu produced four different results in five rounds — illness at 6, a death and heavy expense at 17, high-placed opposition at 41, death at 53. A configuration marks a pressure point; the round and the context decide what comes of it.
Combination of the rule: The reader is tempted to fix one meaning to one configuration.

Rule description: Saturn's rounds: ≈30 years, and they are counted like Jupiter's
Exact rule: The book counts Saturn's rounds explicitly, at ≈2½ years per sign, ≈30 years per round: - Ch 41 — "The conjunction of Mars with Saturn indicates great troubles in the period during the second round of Saturn (i.e., after 38th year). This will be when Saturn moves out of Aquarius." - Ch 46 — "This native will have good time when Saturn transits Leo in his second round which comes at 52-53." - Ch 52 — "when Saturn transits Jupiter in his 2nd round, he will be defamed."
Effect of the rule: Saturn's own long arc across a life, read alongside Jupiter's twelve-year one.
Combination of the rule: Saturn is set walking from his natal sign; a round is one circuit of the zodiac.

Rule description: The SAME contact in a later round gives the OPPOSITE result
Exact rule: The single cleanest proof of RAO-JTC-014 in the corpus. In one chart, in consecutive sentences: "Saturn transits Jupiter, first in Aries. This denotes a position of importance in Government … when Saturn transits Jupiter in his 2nd round, he will be defamed."
Effect of the rule: Office, then defamation — then, when Jupiter transits Virgo and Libra, reinstatement at about 54.
Combination of the rule: A transiting planet contacts the same natal planet on successive rounds.

Rule description: Mercury has his own round, and it times education
Exact rule: "The Mercury transits Saturn and Mars in the course of his rounds. So his educational career will not be smooth and will be full of obstacles."
Effect of the rule: Broken, obstructed education.
Combination of the rule: Mercury set walking forward from his natal sign; note what he meets.

Rule description: Rahu's clock: ≈1½ years per sign, backwards
Exact rule: The book gives the rate explicitly — "The retrograde Rahu takes about 6-7 years to reach the Sun's position in Sagittarius. That will be the time when the father will have many troubles."
Effect of the rule: Rahu-timed events, dated by backward count.
Combination of the rule: Rahu set walking backwards from his natal sign.

Rule description: Education runs on Jupiter's first two rounds, and breaks where he meets Rahu
Exact rule: The most detailed education timeline in the batch, worked as a continuous walk: "The native's education will continue upto 11 when Jupiter transits Rahu and so the native will discontinue his studies. Education will continue in Jupiter's second round from Taurus to Sagittarius and Capricorn. He will have obstructions thereafter. Education will be regularised and will continue till Jupiter reaches Rahu."
Effect of the rule: A two-stage education with breaks at each Jupiter–Rahu contact.
Combination of the rule: Jupiter's itinerary through rounds 1 and 2 is traced sign by sign.

Rule description: A debilitated planet does not fully aspect
Exact rule: The disciple asks what results; "The Master says that Venus does not fully aspect the sign Pisces."
Effect of the rule: A weakened, partial delivery of what the aspect promises.
Combination of the rule: A debilitated planet aspects a sign — here debilitated Venus in Virgo aspecting her own exaltation sign Pisces.

Rule description: The Nth house from Jupiter fires in the Nth year of the round
Exact rule: Two independent statements in one chart, and they settle the arithmetic completely: - "The native represented by Jupiter has Rahu-Moon in 5th house. Therefore, the mother, who gave birth, died in his 5th year." - "About the age of 9-10, the native's father came by vast fortunes … This is due to the Sun conjunction with Mars-Mercury in the 10th house from Jupiter."
Effect of the rule: Practical consequence: whenever Rao names a house from a planet he is simultaneously naming an age. Many statements that look purely positional are also timings — read them both ways.
Combination of the rule: A planet occupies the Nth house counted from natal Jupiter, Jupiter's own sign being the 1st.

Rule description: Combustion: a planet "eclipsed by the Sun" is spoiled
Exact rule: "The promoter of education Mercury is in conjunction with Venus, but both eclipsed by the Sun will cause impediments in education."
Effect of the rule: The eclipsed planet fails to deliver what it signifies.
Combination of the rule: A planet stands with the Sun and is described as eclipsed by him.

Rule description: Saturn's second-round transit over Jupiter: rise, or disgrace
Exact rule: Two charts, the same named transit, opposite results: - Ch 85 — "When Saturn transits Jupiter in his second round the native will rise to a great position." - Ch 52 — "when Saturn transits Jupiter in his 2nd round, he will be defamed."
Effect of the rule: Great rise, or defamation — decided by the frame, not by the contact.
Combination of the rule: Saturn transits natal Jupiter in his second round (≈ ages 30–59).

Rule description: A planet is read for the sign it is about to enter
Exact rule: A general device, confirmed four times: - Ch 100 — "With Ketu behind and the exaltation sign in front, Mercury endows the native with legal knowledge." - Ch 35 — "Next Mercury enters his exaltation in Virgo … the native will receive kingly honours." - Ch 96 — "Here Rahu is moving towards Mars placed in the forest sign." - Ch 10 — "Rahu is about to pounce upon Venus. This indicates a widow."
Effect of the rule: What the planet is approaching colours what it gives.
Combination of the rule: A planet stands immediately before a significant sign, or a node stands immediately before a planet.

Rule description: A retrograde planet acts from the PREVIOUS sign
Exact rule: The general mechanism behind half the corpus's retrogression readings, and it is stated outright: > Ch 131 — "the presence of Jupiter all alone in exaltation in Cancer indicates long life for > the father. Jupiter is, however, retrograde, he therefore gets the Gemini power and his aspect > to the Sun is nullified. So the father will die young." Jupiter stands in Cancer; retrograde, he "gets the Gemini power" — he acts from the sign behind him, and the aspect he would have cast from Cancer is cancelled.
Effect of the rule: The planet delivers from the previous sign; its aspects from its own sign are nullified. Ch 152 works the same device forward: "As Jupiter is retrograde, on his entering Leo, he will aspect Saturn, Venus and the Moon."

Rule description: Exchange of signs creates a VIRTUAL conjunction
Exact rule: The disciple objects that the father can only have had one wife; the Master's answer defines the mechanism. The disciple: "The Sun representing father is conjunct Jupiter and the Moon. All the 3 have no planets in the 7th house to them… Hence I think the native had only one mother." The Master: > "Venus, Lord of both Taurus and Libra … is having exchange of places with Jupiter in Taurus. > So the Sun will have the effect of being conjunct with the Moon and Venus, both female planets. > So the father will marry twice."
Effect of the rule: A conjunction that is not visible in the chart but is read as if it were.
Combination of the rule: Two planets occupy each other's signs.

Rule description: The house-number clock, confirmed four more times
Exact rule: Three more unambiguous instances, and now counted from the Sun as well as from Jupiter: - Ch 114 — "The second house to the Sun and Saturn is occupied by Venus, Mercury and Mars. Therefore, in the second year after the birth of the boy there will be great improvement in father's position." - Ch 119 — "As the Sun has Saturn, Venus and Mercury in the 2nd house to him, the father would have come into possession of great riches in the 2nd year after the boy's birth. In the third and fourth year during Jupiter's contact with Mars in Virgo, he would have come into possession of a house." - Ch 117 — "As the Sun has no benefic planet in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th houses from him, the father will not have any favourable circumstances after the boy completes his 5th year."
Effect of the rule: Every positional statement in this corpus is simultaneously a dated one.
Combination of the rule: A planet occupies the Nth house from a karaka.

Rule description: Rahu swallows what lies behind him
Exact rule: The imagery is consistent and vivid — Rahu is a mouth (RAO-FND-038): - Ch 105 — "Rahu is in Capricorn, about to enter Sagittarius and swallow up Jupiter. So the native will have hard times between the first and second year." - Ch 136 — "Saturn is in Capricorn and Rahu in Aquarius ready to swallow up the former." - Ch 145 — "Saturn, though placed in his own house, is in claws of Rahu crossing from Aquarius." - Ch 143 — "Saturn to enter Rahu's mouth in Aquarius."
Effect of the rule: The swallowed planet's promise is consumed.
Combination of the rule: Rahu stands in the sign after a planet, and so moving backwards is approaching it.

Rule description: "Getting the amsa of the previous sign" — retrogression confirmed in the book's own words
Exact rule: RAO-JTC-025 was derived from Chart 131. Chart 196 states it outright, in a single clause: > "Jupiter in Aquarius is retrograde and getting the amsa of previous sign. The sign Capricorn > falls 7th to Venus and so the father of the native will also be one learned in Vedic literature." The reading then proceeds from Capricorn, the sign behind Jupiter — not from Aquarius.
Effect of the rule: The planet delivers one sign back; displacement in place as well as in position.

Rule description: Exchange as virtual conjunction, confirmed a second time
Exact rule: Chart 194 states the mechanism as flatly as Chart 116 did: > "Mercury has change of places with Mars. This will constitute a conjunction of Mercury and > Venus in Gemini — and so the father would be the head of an institution and will also conduct > money lending." And Chart 187 adds the negative case, which is new: "On account of the exchange of places between Mercury and the Sun, Venus loses his power. On account of this whatever job he will take up will not bring him peace of mind and he will have financial losses."
Effect of the rule: A conjunction that is not in the chart; and collateral loss of power for planets nearby.
Combination of the rule: Two planets occupy each other's signs.

Rule description: A direct aspect outranks a transit contact
Exact rule: A disciple asks why the native does not deal in the trade the contact indicates. The Master's answer establishes a precedence rule the corpus has nowhere else stated: > "One disciple questions why the native did not deal in silks, as Saturn contacts the Sun, > Mercury and Ketu in Gemini as trading sign. The Master answers that he may have trading in > silks as a subsidiary occupation; but as Saturn [is] aspected by Venus and the Moon directly, > his major trade is in drinks."
Effect of the rule: A primary occupation and a secondary one, ranked.
Combination of the rule: A transit contact points to one occupation and a direct aspect points to another.

Rule description: Rahu does no harm in a sign owned by the planet he threatens
Exact rule: The disciple presses the Master on an inconsistency, and gets a clean cancellation rule: > Disciple: "with reference to sisters you stated that they would have lost their husbands > because of the placement of Venus and Rahu. In the case of the native's wife may it not be > predicted similarly?" > Master: "We are dealing with a male chart. In this case, Mars representing male has Venus > next to him and Rahu is placed in the sign of Mars himself. So, Rahu does not do any harm to the > native."
Effect of the rule: The threatened matter escapes.
Combination of the rule: Rahu stands near a karaka, but in a sign owned by that karaka.

Rule description: Exaltation does not guarantee delivery; the contact order overrides it
Exact rule: "Though Venus is in exaltation, he does not help the native to hold a high place, as Venus contacts only Ketu first and Moon next, who will prove more obstructive than helpful."
Effect of the rule: A dignified planet that does not deliver.
Combination of the rule: A planet is exalted, but the planets it meets are obstructive.

Rule description: The saving grace, and the apparent yoga that does not fire
Exact rule: Rao names the mitigator explicitly, and it is a habit worth codifying: - Ch 196 — Mercury in his own sign but with his bitter enemy Mars: "The saving grace is the presence of Venus all alone in the second place to Mercury. This makes the native greatly interested in arts and music." - Ch 166 — "Venus and Jupiter have Rahu in the next house. But, the Sun's position in the same house with Rahu will save the native from several calamities." - Ch 199 — the reverse: an indication that looks decisive and is not. "Jupiter contacts Saturn first and then Ketu. It appears as though there is Sanyas (renunciation) Yoga. But before Jupiter transits Leo, the native will get married."
Effect of the rule: The affliction survives, but reduced; or the apparent yoga does not fire at all.
Combination of the rule: An affliction is read, and a single supporting placement stands against it.

Rule description: Exchange is "tantamount to being stationed there" — and it can save a life
Exact rule: The disciple now states the mechanism himself, as settled doctrine: > "Disciple: As Jupiter and Mercury have exchanged houses, it is tantamount to Jupiter being > stationed in Sagittarius and Mercury in Virgo." > "Preceptor: It is because of the exchange of houses between Jupiter and Mercury that the native > has the prospect of marrying and getting children. Had the exchange of houses not been there, the > native would have died quite early." Ch 270 puts it as arithmetic: "Because of the transposed positions of Venus and Mars, it becomes equivalent to Mars being in the 12th house from Mercury." Ch 215 adds that the dignity travels too: "As there is exchange of place between Mercury and the Moon, Mercury comes by the power of exaltation in Virgo."
Effect of the rule: Read the chart twice: once as drawn, once with the exchanged pair swapped.
Combination of the rule: Two planets occupy each other's signs.

Rule description: Distance to help: empty signs counted as ROUNDS
Exact rule: The book's only fully worked example of this count, and it does NOT use the one-sign-one-year rule: > "Virgo is not a good place for Jupiter … There are no planets in the adjacent two houses. There > are no planets even in the seventh house. Therefore, having no one to care for him, Jupiter turns > back from Virgo in retrogression… But, in Sagittarius, Jupiter has his friend Mars, Ketu and > Mercury. Three houses — Virgo, Libra and Scorpio — have to be passed for Jupiter to find help. > That comes to 3 × 12 = 36 years. So, the native will pass through a dangerous period during > his 36th year."
Effect of the rule: The length of an unsupported karaka's barren stretch. Compare RAO-PRF-021, where the width of the emptiness likewise set the duration.
Combination of the rule: A karaka is unsupported and must travel several signs before reaching a friendly planet.

Rule description: The fallback window: if the event misses its date, it fires later
Exact rule: Rao writes the contingency into the prediction itself: - Ch 250 — "He will undergo a surgical operation during his 38th year and there will be a vehicular accident during his 43rd year. If these incidents do not take place in the said periods, they may occur between 47th and 49th year." - Ch 277 — "the native of such a horoscope will die during his 11th year. If he outlives this age, he will certainly die during his 25th year. In the event of his living upto his 25th year, he will become a father of two children."
Effect of the rule: The event, at one of two named times — or not at all.
Combination of the rule: A dated event does not occur in its stated window.

Rule description: Mutual weakening, and dignity spoiled by retrogression
Exact rule: Three further ways the corpus reduces a planet, added to RAO-KRK-067: - Mutual weakening — Ch 253, "it has to be taken into account that the Sun and Venus mutually weaken each other. This indicates that the native may get government aid but not government service." Note how finely the reduction is expressed: not no government, but aid instead of service. - Retrogression spoils exaltation — Ch 254, "it appears that Jupiter is exalted in Cancer. But, as Jupiter is retrograde, he is not entirely in an exalted state." - Rank in company — RAO-KRK-094.
Effect of the rule: A weakened, downgraded delivery.
Combination of the rule: Two enemies stand together; or a dignified planet is retrograde.

Rule description: Precision finer than the sign: nakshatra, degrees, solar month, weekday
Exact rule: The corpus is overwhelmingly whole-sign (RAO-JTC-002), but it breaks that rule five times in this block, and each break is worth knowing: | Refinement | Statement | Chart | |---|---|---| | Nakshatra | "as Saturn is in the constellation of Ashvini, Ketu and Saturn are quite closely placed" | Ch 230 | | Nakshatra | "Mars is also in Aries in a previous constellation from that of Saturn" | Ch 248 | | Degrees | "The Sun and Venus are located in the same constellation within three degrees of each other. This indicates that the native will have mostly female children" | Ch 265 | | Sign boundary | "Ketu is on the border of Aries and Pisces" | Ch 230 | | Solar month | "During his 26th year between the middle of August and middle of September his fortune will commence improving" | Ch 228 | | Weekday | "during her 58th year, when Jupiter reaches Pisces, will breathe her last on a Tuesday" | Ch 243
Effect of the rule: A sharper position or date where the sign alone will not do.
Combination of the rule: The whole-sign frame is not fine enough to settle a point.

Rule description: The one place Rao prints his arithmetic
Exact rule: The only calculation actually shown as a sum anywhere in the book: > "Saturn meets Rahu after crossing four vacant houses. This is not a happy indication. It > denotes servitude and poverty which will last up to his 38–40th year. When Saturn in his second > round crosses Capricorn he gets the aspect of Venus in Leo, and there will be a change in the > native's life and his prospects will brighten — (30 + 4 × 2 + 2 = 30 + 10 = 40)."
Effect of the rule: The age at which an unsupported karaka finally meets help. The verdict it replaces — "servitude and poverty" — falls squarely under RAO-FND-039 and is never to be delivered.
Combination of the rule: Saturn must cross several vacant signs before reaching any planet.

Rule description: Retrogression: "looks back", "turns back", "moving to" — the case closed
Exact rule: Seven independent statements now, across 250 pages, and the idiom is always spatial and always backwards: | Phrasing | Chart | |---|---| | "getting the amsa of previous sign" | Ch 196 | | "he therefore gets the Gemini power" (from Cancer) | Ch 131 | | "turns back to chastise Ketu in the rear" | Ch 235 | | "as Mars is retrograde he influences the Sun from Sagittarius" (from Capricorn) | Ch 213 | | "Saturn has moved into Aries from Taurus in retrogression" | Ch 248 | | "Venus is retrograde in Capricorn and faces Sagittarius" | Ch 248 | | "Venus is retrograde in Gemini and looks back at the Sun and the Moon in Taurus" | Ch 317 | | "Mars retrograde aspects Venus by moving to Capricorn" | Ch 391
Effect of the rule: Displacement one sign back — in aspect, in reach, and in what the planet can deliver.

Rule description: The Jupiter round formula, printed as a sum
Exact rule: The second and last place Rao prints a calculation — and it is RAO-JTC-001 exactly: > "When Jupiter crosses Capricorn, the native will have great danger to face in life. By the Grace > of God, if he will overcome the danger, the same troubles will arise again at 67 (12 × 5 + 7) > when Jupiter in his sixth round crosses Capricorn."
Effect of the rule: The recurrence of a crisis at the next round.
Combination of the rule: A danger recurs one round later.

Rule description: The Vimshottari apparatus, as the closing section actually uses it
Exact rule: Recorded so the appendix can be read on its own terms: - Starting dasa from the birth nakshatra — "born under the asterism of Krittika, third quarter. The relevant Solar Dasha was for a period of two years" (i.e. the balance remaining). - Balance at birth computed to the month — "the balance in Budha Dasha at the time of birth was 9 years and 6 months." - Bhuktis inside the dasa — "had expired upto a little in Chandra's Bhukthi. There was a balance of one year in Chandra's Bhukhti." - Standard Vimshottari lengths — Mars 7 years, Rahu ("the Dragon's head") 18 years. - The Ascendant used for the physical setting of the birth — "the Ascendant, being Virgo, the native would be born in a street running East to West." - Solar-month precision at the close — "in the solar month of Taurus the native would breathe his last."
Effect of the rule: A dasa-by-dasa life narrative, in place of the transit walk.
Combination of the rule: Only in the closing readings. Never in charts 1–447.

Rule description: Jupiter
Exact rule: Jupiter carries more weight in this book than any other body, because he is at once the subject, the karaka of progeny and the hand of the clock.
Effect of the rule: The native himself · the soul (Ch 1) · children (RAO-FND-010) · Dharma / moral principle (Ch 20) · Vedic lore, scripture, religious learning (Ch 21, 22) · the body's proportion and complexion — exalted Jupiter gives "a well-proportioned body with golden colour" (Ch 9) · the birth environment, read from his neighbours (Ch 7, 8). Epithets Rao uses for him: "life propeller" (Ch 8, 13), "life sustainer" (Ch 7).

Rule description: Saturn
Exact rule: "Saturn is the Lord of Karma (work). He is neither good nor bad. The results depend on the position of Saturn" (RAO-FND-018).
Effect of the rule: Karma, work, profession, employment · Action, paired against Jupiter's Dharma (Ch 20) · the judiciary, disputes, settlements (Ch 3) · service and subordination — Ch 25, "will have to work as subordinate" · low caste when debilitated (Ch 2 — catalogued, not endorsed) · Iswaramsa, the Shiva-portion, when a Saturn sign holds Jupiter or the Moon (Ch 1, 4).

Rule description: The Sun
Exact rule: The father's whole life is read from the Sun outward by the standard frame (RAO-FND-009).
Effect of the rule: The father (RAO-FND-015) · Government, authority, high position — the Sun-Saturn pair "indicates Government" (Ch 5), Sun in own house gives rise (Ch 25) · power that overcomes enemies when exalted (Ch 13) · in a female chart, the giver of children — Ch 24, "the Sun who gives children."

Rule description: The Moon
Exact rule: The mother · the elder sister (RAO-FND-016) · the mind — Cancer is called "the house of mind" (Ch 22) · liquids and drink — Ch 7, Jupiter in Aquarius with the Moon in the 7th gives a birthplace "full of fine drinks" · Parvati, the goddess, in name-derivation (Ch 1) · beauty — Ch 9, the Moon in Virgo, "she will be beautiful."
Effect of the rule: The mother · the elder sister (RAO-FND-016) · the mind — Cancer is called "the house of mind" (Ch 22) · liquids and drink — Ch 7, Jupiter in Aquarius with the Moon in the 7th gives a birthplace "full of fine drinks" · Parvati, the goddess, in name-derivation (Ch 1) · beauty — Ch 9, the Moon in Virgo, "she will be beautiful."

Rule description: Mars
Exact rule: Engineering, machinery, mechanical mastery — Ch 1, "Mars who stands for Engineering and Machinery"; Ch 5, exalted Mercury aspected by Mars "indicates mastery of machinery"; Ch 3, "livelihood through machinery" · brothers, and their fate by his transit order (Ch 7) · the husband / partner in a female chart — Ch 24, "The planet indicating the partner (Mars) is conjunct Rahu" · bravery (Ch 8) · wounds, swelling, blood (Ch 1) · dry wood and timber, with Rahu (Ch 11) · horns, in name-derivation (Ch 1) · agriculture and cultivation — Jupiter in a Mars sign gives birth "to a cultivator" (Ch 13).
Effect of the rule: Engineering, machinery, mechanical mastery — Ch 1, "Mars who stands for Engineering and Machinery"; Ch 5, exalted Mercury aspected by Mars "indicates mastery of machinery"; Ch 3, "livelihood through machinery" · brothers, and their fate by his transit order (Ch 7) · the husband / partner in a female chart — Ch 24, "The planet indicating the partner (Mars) is conjunct Rahu" · bravery (Ch 8) · wounds, swelling, blood (Ch 1) · dry wood and timber, with Rahu (Ch 11) · horns, in name-derivation (Ch 1) · agriculture and cultivation — Jupiter in a Mars sign gives birth "to a cultivator" (Ch 13).

Rule description: Mercury
Exact rule: Education, learning, intelligence · trade and the trader — Ch 6, Mercury in the 2nd to the Sun, "he will be a trader dealing in many things" · accounts, treasury, financial work — Ch 21, "enter into a treasury section"; Ch 25, "employed in an Accounts Department" · writing (Ch 21) · intellectual concerns generally — Ch 25, "Saturn is in Mercury's house" → "employed in an intellectual concern" · languages — Ch 20, Ketu in Mercury's sign Virgo, "well versed in three languages" · law, with Jupiter — Ch 2, Mercury in Aquarius with Jupiter next, "the native will be a legal expert."
Effect of the rule: Education, learning, intelligence · trade and the trader — Ch 6, Mercury in the 2nd to the Sun, "he will be a trader dealing in many things" · accounts, treasury, financial work — Ch 21, "enter into a treasury section"; Ch 25, "employed in an Accounts Department" · writing (Ch 21) · intellectual concerns generally — Ch 25, "Saturn is in Mercury's house" → "employed in an intellectual concern" · languages — Ch 20, Ketu in Mercury's sign Virgo, "well versed in three languages" · law, with Jupiter — Ch 2, Mercury in Aquarius with Jupiter next, "the native will be a legal expert."

Rule description: Venus
Exact rule: The wife / the partner — Ch 5, "Venus representing the native's partner" · marriage itself · the arts — Ch 1, "Venus … stands for Arts"; Ch 22, Mars and Venus in Leo give "the art of painting" · money, jewellery, valuables (Ch 9) · conveyances · dresses, with the Moon (Ch 6) · luxury and display — Ch 1, "Venus who is vain-glorious and so wants a royal type of living" · female siblings in the sibling census (RAO-FND-026).
Effect of the rule: The wife / the partner — Ch 5, "Venus representing the native's partner" · marriage itself · the arts — Ch 1, "Venus … stands for Arts"; Ch 22, Mars and Venus in Leo give "the art of painting" · money, jewellery, valuables (Ch 9) · conveyances · dresses, with the Moon (Ch 6) · luxury and display — Ch 1, "Venus who is vain-glorious and so wants a royal type of living" · female siblings in the sibling census (RAO-FND-026).

Rule description: Rahu
Exact rule: Remember he moves backwards — RAO-JTC-013.
Effect of the rule: Always retrograde, and so an amplifier of trouble (RAO-JTC-012) · the mouth, in name-derivation (Ch 1) · foreign lands and travel (Ch 1) · obstruction, opposition from high places (Ch 1) · endless ambition, immoral acts, robbery, duping others (Ch 11 — catalogued, not endorsed) · the Daityamsa, the demon-portion, when with Mars upon the Moon (Ch 3) · widowhood, when about to fall on Venus (Ch 10) · a dilapidated wall beside the birth-house, with Jupiter (Ch 8) · leprosy, with Mars and the Sun (Ch 9 — catalogued, not endorsed).

Rule description: Ketu
Exact rule: Pilgrimage, holy places, religious travel · a pilgrim centre near the birthplace, when behind Jupiter (Ch 7) · Sanyas / renunciation (Ch 8) · the deity Subramanya, with Jupiter (Ch 6) · the tail, in name-derivation (Ch 1) · obstruction and impediment — Ch 21, Ketu in the 4th from Saturn "will cause impediments all along his life and career"; Ch 25, "Ketu creates obstructions" · intelligence, with Mercury (Ch 5) · languages, in a Mercury sign (Ch 20) · shade cast over a conjunction — Ch 22, Mars and Venus "under the shade of Ketu."
Effect of the rule: Pilgrimage, holy places, religious travel · a pilgrim centre near the birthplace, when behind Jupiter (Ch 7) · Sanyas / renunciation (Ch 8) · the deity Subramanya, with Jupiter (Ch 6) · the tail, in name-derivation (Ch 1) · obstruction and impediment — Ch 21, Ketu in the 4th from Saturn "will cause impediments all along his life and career"; Ch 25, "Ketu creates obstructions" · intelligence, with Mercury (Ch 5) · languages, in a Mercury sign (Ch 20) · shade cast over a conjunction — Ch 22, Mars and Venus "under the shade of Ketu."

Rule description: The sign BEHIND natal Jupiter is the previous birth
Exact rule: The single structural rule of this whole file, and it is stated three times: - Ch 6 — "The native in the previous birth was born when Jupiter was in Cancer (house behind the one occupied in present birth). It is occupied by Mercury. He was a trader in the previous birth and had all kinds of wealth, houses and conveyances." - Ch 10 — "In this case, the native's previous birth is indicated by the placement of Jupiter in Libra, the sign behind the one occupied in the chart." - Ch 11 — "His previous birth is indicated by Gemini and Jupiter. Mars is in Gemini and is aspected by Saturn in the 7th therefrom and Rahu in the twelfth."
Effect of the rule: The occupants of that sign, and the standard frame around it (RAO-FND-009), describe the previous life — its trade, its wealth and its offence.
Combination of the rule: Take the sign immediately before the one Jupiter occupies at birth.

Rule description: The previous birth's offence explains the present life's defect
Exact rule: The causal chain is always stated explicitly, offence → curse → present defect: - Ch 6 — the native, a wealthy trader, saw "a young girl (the Moon just coming out of conjunction with the Sun) at the doorway" and seduced her; the Goddess "gave the native a blow on his back (Jupiter midway between Mercury and Mars)" and cursed him. Consequence: "a dark mark on his back", "plodding on with little income and a perturbed mind", and "he will go on changing professions." - Ch 11 — "He would have done a lot of immoral acts on account of his endless ambitions. He would also have committed robberies and duped many including high government officials." Consequence: "delay in having his own house in this life, father's loss at an early age, enmity with relations, trials and troubles to wife and mother." - Ch 10 — an illicit connection and a poisoning; "For this offence the native had to undergo living in Naraka, and after that got this birth. The remnant effects will give ill-health to his children, trials and troubles in life."
Effect of the rule: The named present-life deficiency, with a cause attached, and a remedy (RAO-PBR-004).
Combination of the rule: An offence is read in the previous-birth sign.

Rule description: The father's previous birth is read the same way, from the Sun
Exact rule: The disciple asks what this signifies; the Master answers that the father "visited the Palani temple. He was induced by his friend to seduce a woman there (Jupiter's conjunction with Ketu indicates the deity Subramanya). As a result of this sinful act, he will be born in a low caste family and undergo trials and tribulations in his life."
Effect of the rule: The father's future birth and its hardship. Note that Jupiter with Ketu identifies the deity of the temple (RAO-KRK-021) — the configuration names the place.
Combination of the rule: The Sun moves to the next sign and exchanges places with the Moon, then contacts Jupiter.

Rule description: Jupiter's neighbours describe the house the native was born in
Exact rule: One of the most striking devices in the book — the frame is read literally, as geography: - Ch 8 — "In this chart, life propeller Jupiter is conjunct Rahu. There will be a dilapidated wall by the side of the house in which the native was born. As Mars is posited next to Jupiter, there will be houses adjoining the birth home." - Ch 7 — "life sustainer Jupiter is in Aquarius and the Moon in the seventh house therefrom. So, the place of birth was full of fine drinks." - Ch 20 — the Sun hemmed between Saturn and Mars: "He was born in a place where there were no neighbours on either side."
Effect of the rule: A physical description of the birthplace, verifiable against family memory — which is precisely why the Nadi tradition uses it as a confirmation test before proceeding to prediction.
Combination of the rule: Read the signs around Jupiter (the native) as the ground around the house.

Rule description: Jupiter in a Mars sign with Ketu in the 2nd: born to a cultivator

Combination of the rule: Jupiter in a sign of Mars, Ketu occupying the 2nd to him.
